title: Reporter's Notebook: France braces for more unrest after parts of Paris spun out of control
summary: French Prime Minister Lecornu says a massive police operation backed by the military will counter the next protest set for this weekend in France.
story: Senior foreign affairs correspondent Greg Palkot reports live from Paris on the spreading violence and curfews in France following days of rioting.
PARIS, France: Paris is burning. Yet again. But this time, according to officials and analysts, it’s different. And unrest here could have a lasting impact on France… perhaps the world.
I have been covering protests in France for decades. I lived in Paris for nine years. I know that the French are very skilled at taking politics to the street. The recent upheaval has many worried.
From all the people I hear from on the ground here, the rioting has been more violent, more destructive, more profound. Domestic strife seemingly out of control.
FRANCE IS DEVOURING ITSELF AS SCHOOL RIOTS REVEAL A CRISIS FAR BIGGER THAN BROKEN CLASSROOMS
Greg Palkot, senior foreign affairs correspondent for Fox News Channel  at the Place de la Republique in Paris. Oct. 19, 2026. (John Templeton/Fox News)

When I approached the bar at a brasserie near Place de la Republique, the server asked if I was an American and a journalist. After replying yes to both he concluded, "So you’ve come to cover the civil war."

The numbers tell the tale. Some 2,500 arrests during the last weekend of clashes between protesters and police. Around 1,000 officers injured. Many hurt, some seriously, on the activists’ side. And about 3,000 businesses impacted, trashed, looted. Damage estimated over one billion dollars.
FRANCE'S MASSIVE INTEL FAILURE SPARKS RESIGNATION OFFERS AMID DAYS OF RIOTING
Graffiti covers an historic monument in the Place de la Republique. Paris, France. Oct 20, 2026. (John Templeton/Fox News)

What was most striking were the attacks on official buildings. An historic city hall in Limoges. A police headquarters in crime-ridden Marseille. An important tourist office in Lyon. Symbols of a French government under siege.

The mostly peaceful protests supporting recent student concerns, as well as working and middle-class economic worries, hijacked by those bent on anarchy. And opportunistic young crooks looking for cheap thrills.

Yes, there are immigrants and foreigners amid the rabble. Plus, those said to have ties with so-called "ultra-left" groupings. But this remains a very French uprising. Which in a way makes it even more unsettling.
Nearly ten years of rule by President Emmanuel Macron has left this country more divided, with promises unfilled, anger near the surface. And violence a real danger.
FRENCH NEWSPAPER RIPS MACRON AFTER RIOTS ERUPT ACROSS FRANCE: ‘INDELIBLE STAIN’
Burned-out cars litter the streets in Paris by the Place de la République (John Templeton/Fox News)

What was also deeply troubling about the latest bout of violence — and authorities have admitted it — is that there were periods of time when parts of Paris and other cities were out of control. Shop owners were forced to fend for themselves.

All of this plum pickings for politicians on the left and right. Either sympathizing with protesters’ demands. Or calling for more law and order. Both sides slamming those in power. With presidential elections upcoming in six months, timing is everything.
With the French treasury bare, it seems the more pressing and more promising route for the current authorities is greater security.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Graffiti on the wall by the Place de la Republique in Paris, France on Oct. 19, 2026. (John Templeton/Fox News)

That’s why top government officials have been speaking out about their planning for the next big protest set for this weekend. French Prime Minister Lecornu says it will be countered by a "massive police operation" backed by the military. Activists will have to choose, Lecornu went on to say, between "violence" and the French "republic."

"Do or die" talk that still does not address the underlying problems, not just facing France but other countries as well. That’s why, in addition to the curiosity factor of everyone being intrigued by France, it could also provide some real-time lessons on how or how not to deal with a brave new world of inequality and dwindling resources.
See you at the "barricades."
Greg Palkot serves as a London-based senior foreign affairs correspondent for FOX News Channel (FNC). He joined the network in 1998 as a correspondent.

title: Sea mine crisis re-emerges in Strait of Hormuz as Tehran urges Washington to accept deal
summary: Iran claims two oil tankers struck sea mines in the Strait of Hormuz as the IMO warns the critical shipping lane remains too unsafe to transit.
story: IMO Secretary-General  Arsenio Dominguez says ships risk hitting mines in Strait of Hormuz as Iran's temporary route lacks international approval

Sea mines have resurfaced as a threat in the Strait of Hormuz, where Iran claimed Oct.17 that two oil tankers caught fire after striking the explosives, raising fresh alarms over the safety of one of the world's most critical shipping lanes.

This came as the International Maritime Organization (IMO) warned that sea mines pose a serious threat to vessels navigating the strategic waterway and while Tehran continues to maintain its own unauthorized shipping corridor inside its territorial waters.

"The traffic separation scheme, the information that we have is that they still have mines. And of course, whilst the conflict is ongoing, it's very difficult for us to use third parties to verify that it is clear of these hazards," IMO Secretary-General Arsenio Dominguez told Fox News Digital.
INSIDE THE DANGEROUS US MISSION THAT CLEARED IRAN’S MINES FROM HORMUZ SHIPPING LANES

Mine countermeasures ship USS Dextrous (MCM 13) (not pictured) sails with ships participating in the Oman-led exercise Khunjar Hadd in the Gulf of Oman. Dextrous is deployed to the U.S. 5th Fleet area of operations to help ensure maritime security and stability in the Middle East Region. (U.S. Naval Forces Central Command/U.S. 5th Fleet/Handout via REUTERS)
"So in the meantime, we cannot guarantee that a vessel that intends to transit that route will not be hit by a mine."

Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) navy said Saturday that two oil tankers caught fire after striking naval mines while crossing the Strait of Hormuz, Reuters reported, citing Iran's official Islamic Republic News Agency (IRNA).
State media also said both tankers were carrying about 2 million barrels of crude oil, according to Reuters.
IRNA also reported that the vessels had switched off their positioning and radar systems and attempted to use a route through the strategic waterway that Iran had not authorized.
IRAN WARNS SHIPS OF 'FORCEFUL RESPONSE' AS US-BACKED HORMUZ ROUTE CHALLENGES TEHRAN'S GRIP
Smoke column rises from tanker El Gaia after incident in Strait of Hormuz
The second tanker was left immobilized after striking a mine, according to the Reuters report.

The alleged strikes came as Tehran continued to maintain its transit passageway inside Iranian territorial waters, imposing tolls and safety fees administered by the IRGC — a framework rejected by Washington and the IMO as inconsistent with international maritime law.
International shipping through the narrow chokepoint has historically relied on an IMO-approved traffic separation scheme adopted in 1968.
"Right now there's only one route that was adopted back in 1968 that is approved and recognized for IMO and that appears in all the charts for the vessels to operate," Dominguez explained.
IRAN FAILS TO STRIKE DEAL WITH US AS DEADLINE PASSES AND TRUMP CALLS FOR ‘WHITE FLAG OF SURRENDER'

Attacks on vessels around the Strait of Hormuz have surged over the past two weeks. Senior Iranian officials also told Reuters that Tehran has shifted its strategy for attacking commercial vessels during that period. (Morteza Nikoubazl/NurPhoto via Getty Images)
"There's only one route that should be used for transit, but it's not clear of mines right now, so it's not safe."

"We have received confirmation from Iran about the establishment of its temporary route in the waters," he added before stating that the route was not provided with "an official confirmation or a decision of the organization."
"Any other route needs to actually be sent to the organization to go through the processes, and we have not received that."
"We have received communication from Iran to use that route because of the conflict," Dominguez clarified.
"That's the way that it's been presented. But anything for us to approve needs to go through the mechanisms at the international maritime organizations and the member states need to review it."
The developments also came amid stalled negotiations between Washington and Tehran over ending the conflict and restoring maritime traffic.
DISTRESS CALL CAPTURES TANKER UNDER FIRE, IRAN SHUTS HORMUZ TRAPPING THOUSANDS OF SAILORS
Basij paramilitary force speed boats are sailing along the Persian Gulf near a general cargo vessel  ( Morteza Nikoubazl/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council and a former Revolutionary Guard commander, said Tehran considered Washington's latest response to negotiations "insufficient," Reuters reported, according to IRNA.

Rezaei said the U.S. had accepted some of Iran's seven conditions but that other issues remained unresolved, adding that Tehran was no longer responding to Washington and that the U.S. needed to clarify the outstanding matters.

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said that Tehran had submitted a proposal to Washington through Qatar, which is mediating the negotiations, outlining conditions under which the Strait of Hormuz could reopen and normal maritime traffic resume within seven days.

"Our situation is clear and based on ⁠the seven-day proposal presented to the US. They shared comments which ​we are reviewing, but our proposal is still on the table ​and if there is any honesty on the US part, which there isn't, the way to reopening the Strait of Hormuz is obvious," Araqchi said in ​Baghdad, Reuters reported
IRAN REQUESTS TALKS WITH US AS WHITE HOUSE WARNS 'VIOLENCE WILL BE MET WITH VIOLENCE'
As U.S.-Iran talks opened Sunday in Switzerland, a dispute over who controls and monitors billions of dollars in potentially unfrozen Iranian assets emerged (Fabrice Coffrini/Pool via REUTERS)
Meanwhile, attacks on commercial vessels around the Strait of Hormuz have surged over the past two weeks.
Senior Iranian officials also told Reuters that Tehran has shifted its strategy for attacking commercial vessels during that period.
For commercial shipping operators, Dominguez warned that the continued threat of mines and attacks means the waterway has yet to return to normal operations.
The Strait of Hormuz is "not open for business in the way that it was before the conflict started," he said.

"Our role right now is to prepare for when we have the opportunity to go back, resume the operations, follow all the procedures at IMO, but not until the root causes are addressed and those are beyond IMO."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Fox News Digital reached out to U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) for comment.

Emma Bussey is a breaking news writer for Fox News Digital. Before joining Fox, she worked at The Telegraph with the U.S. overnight team, across desks including foreign, politics, news, sport and culture.

title: Iran regime under pressure as rebel groups escalate attacks in volatile southeast
summary: A coalition of armed rebel groups is stepping up attacks against Iranian regime forces in the country's volatile southeast, raising questions about Tehran's grip on the region.
story: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu outlines his vision for the future of Iran’s Islamic regime on ‘Life, Liberty & Levin.’

A new coalition of Iranian opposition groups in the restive southeastern provinces of Sistan and Baluchistan and Kerman in the Islamic Republic have launched a string of armed attacks against the clerical regime in the region.

The six strikes claimed by the coalition known as the People’s Fighters Front (JMM) have contributed to instability in the provinces, raising pressing questions about whether armed resistance against the clerical regime in Tehran will spread and if the regime can retain control over Sistan and Baluchistan, which is a majority Iranian Sunni province.
Iran is largely a Shiite Muslim country, and the minority Iranian Sunni population has faced discrimination over the decades. Sistan and Baluchistan is the second largest of the 31 Iranian provinces.
MOJTABA KHAMENEI DEFIES ‘MALICIOUS’ ATTACKS AS US ARMY ZEROES IN ON IRAN’S 350,000 TROOPS
Sistan and Baluchistan, Iran. (Mohammad /Middle East Images/AFP via Getty Images)

Mardo Soghom, an Iran expert who has written extensively about the Islamic Republic, told Fox News Digital, "The Sunni unrest can stretch the regime's military and internal security capabilities and have a psychological impact on its forces, in addition to what they experienced during the 40-day operation by the U.S. and Israel. The armed groups would not be able to establish control of the south-east, but they can seriously weaken the regime's control."
He added, "Whether these forces are receiving assistance from the Islamic Republic's adversaries — being that the Gulf Arab states or even Israel and the U.S. — remains an open question."

Protesters and members of Iranian paramilitary Basij forces march next to the fourth generation Khorramshahr ballistic missile Khaibar displayed during an anti-Israeli rally to show their solidarity with Palestinians in Tehran on Nov. 24, 2023. (Photo by Hossein Beris/Middle East Images/AFP via Getty Images)

According to an October Human Rights Activist News Agency (HRANA) report, "The pace of violence accelerated significantly in recent weeks [in the provinces] with 18 incidents recorded in just the final 18 days of the reporting period, surpassing the total for any previous full month."
JMM coalesced as an opposition coalition in Dec. 2025 through an amalgam of Baloch nationalist organizations with the militant Sunni group Jaish al-Adl.

HRANA documented "at least 63 armed incidents were recorded across Iran’s southeastern provinces of Sistan and Baluchistan and Kerman between March 31 and Oct.10, 2026, amid a sharp escalation in armed violence in the region."
The armed resistance resulted in "at least 94 people dead and 33 injured, while official sources reported 87 fatalities and 10 injuries."
IRAN INSTALLS NEW WAR CHIEFS AS TEHRAN SIGNALS ‘PROLONGED CONFRONTATION,’ EXPERT WARNS

A woman member of the Basij paramilitary, affiliated with Iran's Revolutionary Guard, holds a machine gun on a pickup truck during a parade of pro-government Iranian women. (Sobhan Farajvan/Pacific Press/LightRocket via Getty Images)

The Baloch coalition stunned the regime on Oct. 14 with the assassinations of women members of the Basij paramilitaries, including a commander and a police officer in Sistan and Baluchistan Province. The Basij has been designated a terrorist entity by the U.S. government because it falls under the American-classified terrorist movement Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC).

Just days before the attack on the female Basij commander, Iranian regime-controlled media reported that Nosrat Eftekhari, deputy for Cultural and Social Affairs of the Provincial Law Enforcement Command, was killed by a roadside bomb in Zahedan, Sistan and Baluchistan provinces.

Jason Brodsky, policy director at United Against Nuclear Iran (UANI), told Fox News Digital that "There have been periodic cycles of unrest in Sistan and Baluchistan Province over the years. What we are now witnessing is an uptick in such activity. The current commander of the IRGC’s Ground Forces, Mohammad Karami used to be governor of the province and commanded IRGC forces there. His experience in the province was one of the reasons Karami was elevated to the post in 2025 given the sensitive security situation in the country."

Brodsky continued that "I don’t see any imminent threat in terms of such a seizure of control, but a red line for Iranians, especially in the opposition, is preserving the territorial integrity of Iran. That needs to be understood in Western capitals."
MOTORCYCLE PATROLS SWARM IRANIAN CITIES, CHECKPOINTS RISE AS REGIME BRACES FOR UNREST

The Artesh, Iran's regular military, is separate from the IRGC and its affiliated Basij militia. Its forces operate across four branches: the ground forces, navy, air force and air defense force. (Photo by Morteza Nikoubazl/NurPhoto via Getty Images)
Khalilullah Balochi, who is a Baluch activist and journalist, told Iran International that "The activities of these groups are not new; what is new is the intensification of attacks."
JMM’s devastating attacks targeting the brutal Iranian regime have generated attention from Iranian dissidents and experts.

Navid Mohebbi, who worked as a Persian media analyst for the State Department's Public Affairs Bureau, told Fox News Digital "The newly formed popular Fighters Front has carried out a series of relatively successful attacks against mid-level regime officials and security personnel in Sistan and Baluchistan province in recent months, drawing a degree of public attention. At a time when the regime is executing protesters on a daily basis, the killing of certain mid-ranking security and military operatives has been met with some satisfaction among segments of Iranian society."

He warned, however, that "Nevertheless, the Iranian public remains deeply cautious and largely distrustful of such groups. Two major concerns underpin this distrust: the possibility of separatist ambitions and the influence of radical Islamism, which is fundamentally at odds with the increasingly secular outlook of Iranian society."
AFTER 6 MONTHS OF WAR, US MUST PREPARE FOR A FUTURE AFTER IRAN’S GOVERNMENT FALLS
Iranians gather while blocking a street during a protest in Tehran, Iran on Jan. 9, 2026. (MAHSA/Middle East Images/AFP via Getty Images)

Mohebbi sees encouraging signs from the JMM, including "the coalition’s recent statements, unlike the rhetoric traditionally associated with similar groups, contain no explicit references to Baluch separatism. Instead, the coalition has identified its primary objective as dismantling the system of Velayat-e Faqih (Guardianship of the Islamic Jurist) and liberating the country from its oppression. It has explicitly declared that it seeks ‘an Iran for all Iranians."’

He continued that "The reality is that these groups lack the capacity to confront the regime in conventional warfare. Through guerrilla operations, however, they can inflict significant psychological blows on the regime and its security establishment. Whether their activities can gain traction beyond Sistan and Baluchistan will depend largely on their ability to sustain what appears to be an effort to earn broader public trust."

Beni Sabti, an Iran expert at the Institute for National Security Studies (INSS) in Israel, told Fox News Digital the coalition has "a lot of guns" and created an "armed rebellion" against the Iranian regime in the provinces. He said, however, the armed upheaval is limited to the region Baluchistan.

Sabti, who was born in Tehran, said the clerical regime in the capital Tehran does not exercise solid control over the provinces, which resembles parts of South America where some governments lost sovereignty to militias.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

He said that there are no reporters in the restive region. As a result, it is difficult to secure accurate news. Sabti said the "IRGC has a headquarters there to fight against these Baluchis." The JMM coalition "can only continue to harm the soldiers and, from time to time, kill a commander. There are a lot of these local commanders in Iran. It is not like an air force commander."
Benjamin Weinthal reports on Israel, Iran, Syria, Turkey and Europe. You can follow Benjamin on Twitter @BenWeinthal, and email him at benjamin.weinthal@fox.com

title: Global 'Chaos Inc' grows to 101 groups with plans for new rounds of demonstrations
summary: French leftist groups are planning a new round of mobilizations on Oct. 24 as the "Chaos Inc." red-green alliance of far-left and Islamist groups sweeps across Europe.
story: Fox News Digital senior editor Asra Nomani discusses far-left groups funding French riots, the organizations behind the unrest and the indoctrination of young people around the world on 'America Reports.'
The political theater of "Chaos Inc." is preparing for a "rebellion...sweeping Europe."

Two days after an estimated 500,000 demonstrators poured into streets across France and clashes left parts of Paris and other cities burning, French activists are calling supporters back into the streets Saturday, Oct. 24, for a new protest billed as "Acte II," with 212 "mobilizations" currently planned, according to a digital map of the plans.

title: Democrats ask judge to dismiss Trump administration’s challenge to Alaska Senate race
summary: Attorneys for Alaska’s Democratic Senate candidate Mary Peltola and Senate Democrats filed a motion Friday urging a federal judge to drop the Trump administration’s lawsuit that seeks to block the results of the upcoming election if Republican incumbent Dan S. Sullivan loses.
story: Attorneys for Alaska’s Democratic Senate candidate Mary Peltola and Senate Democrats filed a motion Friday urging a federal judge to drop the Trump administration’s lawsuit that seeks to block the results of the upcoming election if Republican incumbent Dan S. Sullivan loses.

The motion, filed on behalf of Peltola’s campaign and the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee, called the lawsuit filed by the Justice Department “an unprecedented pre-emptive strike on democratic elections.”

“This case directly threatens both Proposed Intervenors’ interests by demanding that defendants refuse to certify the election if, and only if, Peltola wins,” the filing said. “It is part of a nationwide attack on free elections by the federal government, which the DSCC has fought at every turn.”

The Trump administration filed suit against election officials in Alaska Thursday, arguing that candidate Dan J. Sullivan Jr.’s appearance on the ballot could mislead those who wish to vote for Sen. Dan S. Sullivan’s re-election.
The lawsuit came after President Donald Trump repeatedly complained about both the incumbent being threatened by a man with the same name and the state’s use of ranked-choice voting.

“I am very concerned about the Dan S. Sullivan Race for the U.S. Senate in Alaska in that it is totally confusing,” Trump wrote in a Truth Social post Wednesday. “It’s ridiculous that the Court didn’t stop this SCAM.”

The DOJ’s lawsuit asks the court to block the Alaska Senate results from being certified if Dan S. Sullivan does not win the election, and if “had all votes cast for Dan J. Sullivan been cast instead for Senator Sullivan and Alaska’s rank-choice process played out accordingly, Senator Sullivan would have won the election.”

The filing from Peltola and Senate Democrats pushes back against this request, stating that “the Department of Justice’s assumption that every voter who casts a vote for Dan J. Sullivan really meant to vote for Senator Sullivan is insulting to voters and irreconcilable with Alaska’s ranked choice voting procedures and the ballot’s clear differentiation between the two candidates.”

“Alaskans for Mary and DSCC are entitled to intervene as of right to defend against the Department of Justice’s extraordinary assault,” the motion said. “And there is reason to doubt that the existing defendants will vigorously defend against DOJ’s demands, given their effort to exclude Daniel J. Sullivan from the ballot earlier this year.”

After Dan J. Sullivan Jr. was removed from the ballot in June after election officials decided his candidacy was “not in good faith,” a judge in Alaska overturned the decision later that month, validating his campaign.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
Trump has claimed that Dan J. Sullivan Jr. is only running because “Democrats put him up as a matter of confusion,” calling his candidacy “corrupt.” Dan J. Sullivan Jr. has denied the allegations.

NBC News reported in July that federal and state investigators were looking into whether Dan J. Sullivan Jr. could be part of a conspiracy to confuse voters, according to two people who had knowledge of the situation.
The DOJ’s lawsuit comes less than two weeks ahead of Election Day and after the state has begun early voting. The court has not yet set a hearing date for the suit.
Legal and election experts told NBC News that the DOJ’s case is on shaky ground.
As U.S. elections are run and certified by state and local officials, rather than the federal government, the law limits the Justice Department’s role in elections.

The nonpartisan Cook Political Report rated the Alaska Senate contest as a “toss-up.” The race marks a critical opportunity for Democrats to take a seat from Republicans as they vie for control of the Senate.

title: How Democrats could win the House, how the GOP could hang on, and where to look for a wave
summary: Three 2026 election scenarios that show which party could end up in control of the U.S. House of Representatives.
story: In 2024, America swung to the right, powering Donald Trump back to the White House with the popular vote behind him and his Republican Party winning majorities in both the House and Senate.

Just two years later, the country appears to be shifting in the opposite direction. Midterm elections are almost always a referendum on the party in power in Washington, and Democrats hope to capitalize on deep voter dissatisfaction with the president’s job performance and what they’ve framed as a crisis of affordability that Republicans have done little to abate. The battle for the Senate, always more of an uphill climb for Democrats to win, appears close, with limited public polling showing tight contests in a number of key states.

The House, however, appears to be Democrats’ to lose. Democrats could add anywhere from a handful of seats to several dozen to their count, according to an NBC News Decision Desk analysis of three different indicators of the national political environment.

But it’s not impossible that Republicans could hang on — or at least, prevent the Democratic Party from running up the score — thanks to a friendlier map bolstered by Trump’s redistricting push. Most Republican-held seats are in districts Trump won by double digits in 2024, meaning Democrats will have to reach further into states and districts Trump won to make big gains.

And while elections are more nationalized today than in the past, not every district will see its vote results shift perfectly in line with the national trend. The individual characteristics of a district, as well as what voters there care about, play an important role in determining a winner. The candidates themselves matter, too, and incumbency can still be a powerful advantage for those seeking re-election.

Even so, looking ahead to how House control could play out on election night requires making an assumption about the size of the national partisan shift toward Democrats, and away from the baseline set by 2024. For our analysis, we examine three ways of estimating that shift: recent polling data, past vote patterns and special election results.

title: 12 injured, including several minors, in shooting near Florida A&M University stadium
summary: Twelve people, including several minors, were injured in a shooting near Florida A&M University’s Bragg Memorial Stadium, where homecoming celebrations included a football game Saturday.
story: Twelve people, including several minors, were injured in a shooting near Florida A&M University’s Bragg Memorial Stadium, where homecoming celebrations included a football game Saturday.

The Tallahassee Police Department said in a statement that 11 of the 12 were shot and that three victims had serious injuries, with one minor in serious condition. The others, it said, were in stable condition.
Six of the injured are under 18 years old and the youngest is 11 years old, Chief Lawrence Revell of the Tallahassee Police Department said at a press conference early Sunday morning.
“Our preliminary information shows that an altercation occurred between individuals,” he added, describing it as “an isolated incident between two or three individuals.”
Revell said that no arrests had yet been made, nor anyone taken into custody, but that police believed one shooter was involved.
“Our priority is to determine what happened and why it happened, and to bring the people that are responsible for this to justice,” he added, asking any witnesses to come forward.

The violence unfolded about 8 p.m. at an intersection adjacent to Bragg Memorial Stadium, it said. Early in the evening, Florida A&M’s Rattlers hosted the Arkansas-Pine Bluff Golden Lions for the historically Black university’s annual homecoming game.
After the shooting took place, the university issued a statement on X asking members of its campus community to stay away from the area.
It described the shooting as having taken place “near campus,” which it said was safe.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
“Our hearts are with the victims and everyone affected by tonight’s incident on Perry Street,” the university said.
Florida State University, about a mile away from Florida A&M, issued an emergency alert about the violence and said it didn’t appear anyone from its school community was involved.
“As a precaution, students, faculty and staff in the Tallahassee area are advised to remain indoors this evening and stay alert,” it said.

Revell offered condolences to the victims and their families, and also praised officers who he said ran without hesitation “into the middle of this, still not knowing where the shooters were, still not knowing how many victims we had.”
“We had officers that were picking up victims and carrying them in their arms to transport victims because they couldn’t get through the mass of people,” he said.
The investigation into the violence was ongoing, and police asked witnesses to come forward.

title: Elon Musk says SpaceX closed Ukraine Starlink ‘loophole’
summary: Elon Musk has said his company imposed limits on the use of its Starlink satellite system in Ukraine last week, after curbs led to disruption to Ukrainian military operations.
story: Elon Musk has said his company imposed limits on the use of its Starlink satellite system in Ukraine last week, after curbs led to disruption to Ukrainian military operations.

Ukraine said Saturday that both Starlink, run by Musk’s SpaceX, and its military variant Starshield were now fully functional after the long outage, two days after President Donald Trump indicated Musk had been asked to “put it back.”
In a series of posts on X on Saturday night into Sunday morning, Musk accused Ukraine of violating “Starlink terms of service” by using it for offensive drone strikes.
“That loophole was closed last week,” the billionaire wrote.
“Using Starlink, a civilian commercial service, for offensive drone strikes to kill people has never been allowed, nor should it be,” he added.
In a separate post, he said: “We simply enforced our terms of service when they were bypassed.”
SpaceX did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Neither Musk nor the United States government ​had initially taken responsibility for imposing the curbs last week, with Musk saying previously with respect to Starshield that “any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS.”
Trump says he 'wasn't involved' in limiting Ukraine's Starlink access

Starlink technology has been critical to frontline communications and Ukraine’s ability to intercept jet-powered drones since Russia launched a full-scale invasion of the country in 2022. Ukraine does not rely on the systems for long-range drone operations within Russia, though it is used for military operations in Ukrainian territories unlawfully annexed by Russia.

Ukrainian officials said the restrictions were imposed without warning and capped Starshield operations at speeds of 100 mph, hampering the military’s ability to intercept drones and forcing the cancellation of some operations.

“Starlink remains critical to the defense of Ukraine, as it is the only system that cannot be jammed or blown up, at least for now,” Musk said. “Were Starlink to be turned off, the Ukrainian front line would collapse immediately. This is NOT a threat, it is simply a statement of fact.”
In a series of posts and replies, he called his critics “bloodthirsty warmongers” who “want the war to continue until every last man in Ukraine has died in a ditch.”
Hours later, responding to an X user comment that said “Zelensky needs to go,” Musk responded: “Yes.”

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Starlink speeds started returning to normal on Saturday night. Ukraine’s defense ministry said Saturday that the connection remained stable at over 250mph. The Ukrainian military does not disclose the systems’ maximum operating speeds.
Russia has barraged Ukraine over the past week, Zelenskyy said on Sunday, though he did not draw any direct link to the limitations.

“This past week alone, Russia has launched around 1,600 guided aerial bombs, 48 missiles of various types, including ballistic missiles, and nearly 2,300 attack drones against Ukraine. Unfortunately, almost every day, these brutal strikes leave people killed and injured,” he said in a post on X.

The restrictions on Starlink services last week came amid a souring of relations between the White House and Ukraine, after President Donald Trump agreed to a diesel deal with Russia, waived sweeping sanctions, and called for Ukraine to get a new president.
The disruption to the service also coincided with what Ukrainian officials described as a temporary interruption to U.S. intelligence warnings about incoming Russian attacks.
In a response to Musk on Sunday, Ukrainian presidential adviser Serhiy Beskrestnov said Sunday that “It’s very strange that Elon Musk doesn’t know about the restrictions on Starlink in Ukraine.”
“Starlink does not work over Russian territory,” he said in a post on Telegram. “So we PHYSICALLY CANNOT USE COMMERCIAL STARLINK for deep strikes and mid-range strikes.”
Serhii Sternenko, a former drone adviser to Ukraine’s defense ministry, said that using a civilian Starlink service for drone missions like Musk had described was “technically impossible.”

“For any satellite terminal to work while on the move, it had to be added to a special list and connected to the military Starshield system,” he posted on X. “All drone missions that required satellite communication could only be carried out using Starshield.”
He added: “We are very grateful to the United States and SpaceX for access to critically important satellite communications. Ukraine did not violate the terms of use.”
Ukrainian drone strikes deep within Russia have continued over the past week despite the Starlink issues.

Asked whether he thought Trump or Musk had directly made the decision to limit Starlink, Zelenskyy told NBC News’ “Meet the Press” last week he did not know but thought “both” were involved. He said that if Trump decided tomorrow to lift the restriction, “it will immediately work as it was before.”

Asked whether he spoke to Musk on Thursday, Trump said: “I don’t want to comment on it, whether I called or whether somebody else called, doesn’t make any difference, I guess. The bottom line — he put it back.”
Even before the latest dispute, there had been signs that Ukraine is keen for more control over its communications.

Earlier this month, the country’s defense ministry announced a partnership with Nokia and Finnish satellite imagery firm ICEYE to develop a “sovereign satellite communications” system, with the two firms already working on building a Starlink-style satellite internet system “built on trusted European technology.”
“Modern warfare has proven that reliable communications are a matter of national security,” Zelenskyy said of the deal at the time. “We must all rely on capabilities that we can control.”

There have been concerns over potential interference with Ukraine’s Starlink connection before, with a September 2022 interruption occurring during a pivotal push by Ukraine to retake territory from Russia.

A Reuters report in 2025 cited three sources who alleged that Musk gave an order that disrupted the counteroffensive, triggering a communication blackout and leaving long-range artillery units reliant on Starlink struggling to hit their targets.
A SpaceX spokesperson called the news agency’s reporting “inaccurate.”

Before the latest collapse in relations with Washington, Ukraine’s military had been chipping away at land seized by Russia in the eastern Donetsk region, part of the Donbas heartland that the Kremlin has been struggling to fully capture.

In one major operation, more than 100 square miles of territory and 16 settlements have been reclaimed, Ukrainian officials have said, crediting methods like using bomber drones to fly robot vehicles behind enemy lines.

title: Elon Musk says SpaceX closed Ukraine Starlink ‘loophole’
summary: Elon Musk has said his company imposed limits on the use of its Starlink satellite system in Ukraine last week, after curbs led to disruption to Ukrainian military operations.
story: Elon Musk has said his company imposed limits on the use of its Starlink satellite system in Ukraine last week, after curbs led to disruption to Ukrainian military operations.

Ukraine said Saturday that both Starlink, run by Musk’s SpaceX, and its military variant Starshield were now fully functional after the long outage, two days after President Donald Trump indicated Musk had been asked to “put it back.”
In a series of posts on X on Saturday night into Sunday morning, Musk accused Ukraine of violating “Starlink terms of service” by using it for offensive drone strikes.
“That loophole was closed last week,” the billionaire wrote.
“Using Starlink, a civilian commercial service, for offensive drone strikes to kill people has never been allowed, nor should it be,” he added.
In a separate post, he said: “We simply enforced our terms of service when they were bypassed.”
SpaceX did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Neither Musk nor the United States government ​had initially taken responsibility for imposing the curbs last week, with Musk saying previously with respect to Starshield that “any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS.”
Trump says he 'wasn't involved' in limiting Ukraine's Starlink access

Starlink technology has been critical to frontline communications and Ukraine’s ability to intercept jet-powered drones since Russia launched a full-scale invasion of the country in 2022. Ukraine does not rely on the systems for long-range drone operations within Russia, though it is used for military operations in Ukrainian territories unlawfully annexed by Russia.

Ukrainian officials said the restrictions were imposed without warning and capped Starshield operations at speeds of 100 mph, hampering the military’s ability to intercept drones and forcing the cancellation of some operations.

“Starlink remains critical to the defense of Ukraine, as it is the only system that cannot be jammed or blown up, at least for now,” Musk said. “Were Starlink to be turned off, the Ukrainian front line would collapse immediately. This is NOT a threat, it is simply a statement of fact.”
In a series of posts and replies, he called his critics “bloodthirsty warmongers” who “want the war to continue until every last man in Ukraine has died in a ditch.”
Hours later, responding to an X user comment that said “Zelensky needs to go,” Musk responded: “Yes.”

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Starlink speeds started returning to normal on Saturday night. Ukraine’s defense ministry said Saturday that the connection remained stable at over 250mph. The Ukrainian military does not disclose the systems’ maximum operating speeds.
Russia has barraged Ukraine over the past week, Zelenskyy said on Sunday, though he did not draw any direct link to the limitations.

“This past week alone, Russia has launched around 1,600 guided aerial bombs, 48 missiles of various types, including ballistic missiles, and nearly 2,300 attack drones against Ukraine. Unfortunately, almost every day, these brutal strikes leave people killed and injured,” he said in a post on X.

The restrictions on Starlink services last week came amid a souring of relations between the White House and Ukraine, after President Donald Trump agreed to a diesel deal with Russia, waived sweeping sanctions, and called for Ukraine to get a new president.
The disruption to the service also coincided with what Ukrainian officials described as a temporary interruption to U.S. intelligence warnings about incoming Russian attacks.
In a response to Musk on Sunday, Ukrainian presidential adviser Serhiy Beskrestnov said Sunday that “It’s very strange that Elon Musk doesn’t know about the restrictions on Starlink in Ukraine.”
“Starlink does not work over Russian territory,” he said in a post on Telegram. “So we PHYSICALLY CANNOT USE COMMERCIAL STARLINK for deep strikes and mid-range strikes.”
Serhii Sternenko, a former drone adviser to Ukraine’s defense ministry, said that using a civilian Starlink service for drone missions like Musk had described was “technically impossible.”

“For any satellite terminal to work while on the move, it had to be added to a special list and connected to the military Starshield system,” he posted on X. “All drone missions that required satellite communication could only be carried out using Starshield.”
He added: “We are very grateful to the United States and SpaceX for access to critically important satellite communications. Ukraine did not violate the terms of use.”
Ukrainian drone strikes deep within Russia have continued over the past week despite the Starlink issues.

Asked whether he thought Trump or Musk had directly made the decision to limit Starlink, Zelenskyy told NBC News’ “Meet the Press” last week he did not know but thought “both” were involved. He said that if Trump decided tomorrow to lift the restriction, “it will immediately work as it was before.”

Asked whether he spoke to Musk on Thursday, Trump said: “I don’t want to comment on it, whether I called or whether somebody else called, doesn’t make any difference, I guess. The bottom line — he put it back.”
Even before the latest dispute, there had been signs that Ukraine is keen for more control over its communications.

Earlier this month, the country’s defense ministry announced a partnership with Nokia and Finnish satellite imagery firm ICEYE to develop a “sovereign satellite communications” system, with the two firms already working on building a Starlink-style satellite internet system “built on trusted European technology.”
“Modern warfare has proven that reliable communications are a matter of national security,” Zelenskyy said of the deal at the time. “We must all rely on capabilities that we can control.”

There have been concerns over potential interference with Ukraine’s Starlink connection before, with a September 2022 interruption occurring during a pivotal push by Ukraine to retake territory from Russia.

A Reuters report in 2025 cited three sources who alleged that Musk gave an order that disrupted the counteroffensive, triggering a communication blackout and leaving long-range artillery units reliant on Starlink struggling to hit their targets.
A SpaceX spokesperson called the news agency’s reporting “inaccurate.”

Before the latest collapse in relations with Washington, Ukraine’s military had been chipping away at land seized by Russia in the eastern Donetsk region, part of the Donbas heartland that the Kremlin has been struggling to fully capture.

In one major operation, more than 100 square miles of territory and 16 settlements have been reclaimed, Ukrainian officials have said, crediting methods like using bomber drones to fly robot vehicles behind enemy lines.

title: 12 injured, including several minors, in shooting near Florida A&M University stadium
summary: Twelve people, including several minors, were injured in a shooting near Florida A&M University’s Bragg Memorial Stadium, where homecoming celebrations included a football game Saturday.
story: Twelve people, including several minors, were injured in a shooting near Florida A&M University’s Bragg Memorial Stadium, where homecoming celebrations included a football game Saturday.

The Tallahassee Police Department said in a statement that 11 of the 12 were shot and that three victims had serious injuries, with one minor in serious condition. The others, it said, were in stable condition.
Six of the injured are under 18 years old and the youngest is 11 years old, Chief Lawrence Revell of the Tallahassee Police Department said at a press conference early Sunday morning.
“Our preliminary information shows that an altercation occurred between individuals,” he added, describing it as “an isolated incident between two or three individuals.”
Revell said that no arrests had yet been made, nor anyone taken into custody, but that police believed one shooter was involved.
“Our priority is to determine what happened and why it happened, and to bring the people that are responsible for this to justice,” he added, asking any witnesses to come forward.

The violence unfolded about 8 p.m. at an intersection adjacent to Bragg Memorial Stadium, it said. Early in the evening, Florida A&M’s Rattlers hosted the Arkansas-Pine Bluff Golden Lions for the historically Black university’s annual homecoming game.
After the shooting took place, the university issued a statement on X asking members of its campus community to stay away from the area.
It described the shooting as having taken place “near campus,” which it said was safe.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
“Our hearts are with the victims and everyone affected by tonight’s incident on Perry Street,” the university said.
Florida State University, about a mile away from Florida A&M, issued an emergency alert about the violence and said it didn’t appear anyone from its school community was involved.
“As a precaution, students, faculty and staff in the Tallahassee area are advised to remain indoors this evening and stay alert,” it said.

Revell offered condolences to the victims and their families, and also praised officers who he said ran without hesitation “into the middle of this, still not knowing where the shooters were, still not knowing how many victims we had.”
“We had officers that were picking up victims and carrying them in their arms to transport victims because they couldn’t get through the mass of people,” he said.
The investigation into the violence was ongoing, and police asked witnesses to come forward.

title: Democrats ask judge to dismiss Trump administration’s challenge to Alaska Senate race
summary: Attorneys for Alaska’s Democratic Senate candidate Mary Peltola and Senate Democrats filed a motion Friday urging a federal judge to drop the Trump administration’s lawsuit that seeks to block the results of the upcoming election if Republican incumbent Dan S. Sullivan loses.
story: Attorneys for Alaska’s Democratic Senate candidate Mary Peltola and Senate Democrats filed a motion Friday urging a federal judge to drop the Trump administration’s lawsuit that seeks to block the results of the upcoming election if Republican incumbent Dan S. Sullivan loses.

The motion, filed on behalf of Peltola’s campaign and the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee, called the lawsuit filed by the Justice Department “an unprecedented pre-emptive strike on democratic elections.”

“This case directly threatens both Proposed Intervenors’ interests by demanding that defendants refuse to certify the election if, and only if, Peltola wins,” the filing said. “It is part of a nationwide attack on free elections by the federal government, which the DSCC has fought at every turn.”

The Trump administration filed suit against election officials in Alaska Thursday, arguing that candidate Dan J. Sullivan Jr.’s appearance on the ballot could mislead those who wish to vote for Sen. Dan S. Sullivan’s re-election.
The lawsuit came after President Donald Trump repeatedly complained about both the incumbent being threatened by a man with the same name and the state’s use of ranked-choice voting.

“I am very concerned about the Dan S. Sullivan Race for the U.S. Senate in Alaska in that it is totally confusing,” Trump wrote in a Truth Social post Wednesday. “It’s ridiculous that the Court didn’t stop this SCAM.”

The DOJ’s lawsuit asks the court to block the Alaska Senate results from being certified if Dan S. Sullivan does not win the election, and if “had all votes cast for Dan J. Sullivan been cast instead for Senator Sullivan and Alaska’s rank-choice process played out accordingly, Senator Sullivan would have won the election.”

The filing from Peltola and Senate Democrats pushes back against this request, stating that “the Department of Justice’s assumption that every voter who casts a vote for Dan J. Sullivan really meant to vote for Senator Sullivan is insulting to voters and irreconcilable with Alaska’s ranked choice voting procedures and the ballot’s clear differentiation between the two candidates.”

“Alaskans for Mary and DSCC are entitled to intervene as of right to defend against the Department of Justice’s extraordinary assault,” the motion said. “And there is reason to doubt that the existing defendants will vigorously defend against DOJ’s demands, given their effort to exclude Daniel J. Sullivan from the ballot earlier this year.”

After Dan J. Sullivan Jr. was removed from the ballot in June after election officials decided his candidacy was “not in good faith,” a judge in Alaska overturned the decision later that month, validating his campaign.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
Trump has claimed that Dan J. Sullivan Jr. is only running because “Democrats put him up as a matter of confusion,” calling his candidacy “corrupt.” Dan J. Sullivan Jr. has denied the allegations.

NBC News reported in July that federal and state investigators were looking into whether Dan J. Sullivan Jr. could be part of a conspiracy to confuse voters, according to two people who had knowledge of the situation.
The DOJ’s lawsuit comes less than two weeks ahead of Election Day and after the state has begun early voting. The court has not yet set a hearing date for the suit.
Legal and election experts told NBC News that the DOJ’s case is on shaky ground.
As U.S. elections are run and certified by state and local officials, rather than the federal government, the law limits the Justice Department’s role in elections.

The nonpartisan Cook Political Report rated the Alaska Senate contest as a “toss-up.” The race marks a critical opportunity for Democrats to take a seat from Republicans as they vie for control of the Senate.

title: Suspect in St. Louis teen’s fatal freeway shooting investigated in another roadway attack
summary: The suspect in the fatal freeway shooting of a high school girl just outside St. Louis is being investigated in connection with a second roadway shooting, court documents show.
story: The suspect in the fatal freeway shooting of a high school girl just outside St. Louis is being investigated in connection with a second roadway shooting, federal court documents show.

Willie Herndon, a 42-year-old from Arlington, Texas, is accused of  killing 17-year-old Alyssa Wilson on Oct. 14. In a federal complaint, investigators say a spent shell casing matching the one used in Alyssa’s shooting was found close to where a vehicle was struck on another freeway three days earlier.

No one was reported injured in the Oct. 11 shooting in St. Louis proper. The federal complaint, filed in U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Illinois, states that a vehicle that had just exited Interstate 55 was hit by gunfire, and that security video showed a white SUV parked on the side of the interstate at the time before it “fled the scene immediately after the shooting.”

“A single cartridge case was recovered,” the federal complaint states. “The cartridge case’s headstamp was the same manufacturer as the one recovered by investigators during Wilson’s murder investigation.”
Lab testing is being conducted to determine if ballistic evidence ties the two crimes, according to the complaint.

Herndon is scheduled to appear in U.S. District Court in East St. Louis on Tuesday for a hearing on his pretrial detention on a federal charge of being a felon with a gun, according to the documents, which state he was convicted of felonies in Los Angeles for taking a vehicle without consent in 2001 and for receiving known stolen property and burglary in 2015.
Herndon is also scheduled to appear at a preliminary hearing on Nov. 4 in the same courthouse.
His federal public defender did not respond to a request for comment.
A high schooler’s life cut short

Herndon was charged with first-degree murder and armed criminal action after his arrest in the killing of Alyssa, a high schooler from nearby Florissant, Missouri, who was driving to a St. Louis Zoo Halloween celebration when she was shot Oct. 14.
“Alyssa was 17, excited about her life, excited about her future,” her father, Robert Hickman, said at a news conference Monday. “This was a senseless act.”
Herndon’s wife, Taiya Herndon, allegedly drove the pair to an Illinois hotel roughly 12 miles from St. Louis after the attack, authorities said. She faces a state charge of hindering prosecution.
Authorities have said Alyssa had no ties to the pair.
It’s not clear if either defendant has been assigned counsel in the state cases. The public defender’s office for the St. Louis area did not respond to a request for comment.
Following a search of the Herndons’ nearby Illinois hotel room after the attack, authorities said they found notebooks with handwritten entries, according to the federal criminal complaint.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
The entries included license plate numbers, descriptions of vehicles and descriptions of law enforcement personnel Willie Herndon believed were following him, the complaint said.

On Oct. 2, the Herndons drove from Texas to Arkansas and then Missouri, arriving the next day, while using one of multiple Oklahoma license plates that did not belong to their white SUV, prosecutors alleged in the complaint. One plate was switched following Alyssa’s shooting, they said.
Killing captured on security video

Investigators relying on security video of the Oct. 14 attack said during Monday’s news conference someone in a white Buick Enclave stopped on the shoulder of the southbound side of Interstate 170 in Overland, Missouri, just outside St. Louis. That person got out, paced around and ultimately opened fire on Alyssa’s vehicle as it passed, authorities said.

A single round penetrated the back of Alyssa’s vehicle and struck the teenager in the back, exiting through her chest, according to the federal complaint against Willie Herndon. She was 12 minutes into her journey to meet a friend at the zoo, it said.
Alyssa was ultimately rushed to Barnes-Jewish Hospital in St. Louis, where she was pronounced dead, officials said.

Using information from security video, including a license plate number for the white Buick and an Arkansas Razorbacks sticker on its liftgate, authorities tracked the SUV to a Days Inn in Caseyville, Illinois, where detectives spent hours staking it out on Oct. 15 and 16, authorities have said.
When Taiya Herndon approached the vehicle, authorities rushed her, they said. When Willie Herndon soon emerged from the hotel afterward, authorities said, he ran and was also taken into custody.
Matching shell casings
The criminal complaint against Taiya Herndon stated that Willie Herndon admitted to investigators that he opened fire on the side of the freeway on Oct. 14, and that she admitted to driving.

“When interviewed, Willie Herndon admitted to standing outside the passenger door of the vehicle on southbound Interstate 170, and discharging a rifle,” the state complaint states. “Taiya Hendon admitted to driving the white Buick Enclave.”
A search of the Herndons’ hotel room turned up an American Built Custom Rifle Company version of the AR-15, a semiautomatic rifle, according to the federal criminal complaint.

It was loaded with MaxxTech 23 7.62x39 ammunition, which matches the brand and size of spent shell casing investigators said they found at the side of Interstate 170 after the attack on Alyssa, according to the federal complaint. MaxxTech was also the maker of the spent casing found near the Oct. 11 attack, it said.

Taiya Herndon is scheduled to appear for a hearing over the amount of her bail, set at $500,000 to be paid in full, on Thursday. Her preliminary hearing is scheduled for Nov. 19, according to state court records.

title: Obama seeks to shore up Abdul El-Sayed with Black voters at Michigan rally
summary: Former President Barack Obama rallied for Michigan’s Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed in Detroit on Saturday as the bitterly fought contest could come down to the city’s substantial Black vote.
story: Former President Barack Obama rallied for Michigan’s Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed in Detroit on Saturday as the bitterly fought contest could come down to the city’s substantial Black vote.

“We’re clear about the choice in this election,” Obama said. “Abdul is fighting for change, real change, change that will bring an end to this war. Change that will get money out of politics and put money in your pocket. Change that will finish the job we started with the Affordable Care Act and guarantee quality, affordable healthcare to every single American.”
“You hear people say this is somehow radical,” Obama continued. “What is radical about that?”
The former president, who rallied earlier Saturday in Cleveland, was joined by El-Sayed, gubernatorial nominee Jocelyn Benson and downballot Democrats less than two weeks before Election Day.

Like his speech earlier in the day, Obama lambasted President Donald Trump and congressional Republicans for “broken promises” made during their 2024 campaigns and criticized Trump’s handling of the Iran war and tariffs, both of which he said have had an outsize effect on Michigan.

story: A man was arrested Friday night near the Brooklyn set of “Miami Vice ’85,” a film starring Michael B. Jordan and Austin Butler.

Alex Perez, 23, of Brooklyn, was arrested just after 11 p.m. on accusations that he displayed a knife during a verbal dispute with another man in the area of Avenue N and McDonald Avenue, the New York City Police Department said.

title: Obama describes Trump as an agent of ‘chaos and cruelty’ in midterm elections pitch
summary: Former President Barack Obama characterized President Donald Trump as an agent of “chaos and cruelty” and a man of broken promises during a midterm election rally.
story: CLEVELAND — Former President Barack Obama, appearing here Saturday at his first campaign rally for this fall’s midterm elections, characterized President Donald Trump as an agent of “chaos and cruelty” and a man of broken promises.
And in a particularly pointed criticism of his Republican successor, Obama mocked Trump’s ballroom construction and the gold accents he has added throughout the White House.

“Does anybody really think this guy in the White House right now is spending all that time thinking about these issues?” Obama wondered. “I mean, I don’t know if you’ve noticed, but he seems very focused on home renovations. He should be on HGTV.”
Obama added a moment later: “He’s got the White House looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory.”

The crowd inside a near-capacity Public Auditorium, which holds more than 10,000, erupted with laughter at that and other quips Obama offered throughout his afternoon address. The former president’s visit was aimed at boosting two Democrats: Amy Acton, the party’s nominee for governor, and former Sen. Sherrod Brown, who has mounted a comeback bid for his old job.

title: Over 4 million tubes of toothpaste have been recalled, including several kids brands
summary: More than 4.3 million tubes of fluoride toothpaste, including Brush Buddies Hot Wheels, Crayola and My Little Pony, were recalled. Here’s how to check your tubes.
story: More than 4.3 million tubes of fluoride toothpaste — many of them kid-themed, in flavors like bubble gum, strawberry and watermelon — have been voluntarily recalled nationwide after the Food and Drug Administration flagged manufacturing problems at the facility that made them.

The recall covers several brands sold under licensed character names, along with a handful of lesser-known labels, and includes tubes with expiration dates stretching into mid-2028, meaning some of the affected toothpaste could be sitting in your medicine cabinet right now.

No illnesses or injuries have been reported. Still, the FDA says families should check lot numbers and expiration dates to see whether their toothpaste is part of the recall. Below, I break down exactly which products are affected, how to tell if you have one and what to do next.
Why were more than 4 million tubes of toothpaste recalled?

The FDA announced the recall of more than 4.3 million tubes of fluoride toothpaste distributed nationwide because of current good manufacturing practice deviations. Those are federal standards meant to ensure products are made consistently and safely, so a deviation means the manufacturing process didn’t meet requirements, not necessarily that the toothpaste itself is harmful.

The voluntary recall was initiated on September 10 by Pritam International Private Limited, an India-based manufacturer, and the FDA classified it as Class II recall on October 19. A Class II recall is for products that could cause temporary or medically reversible health problems, where the chance of serious harm is considered unlikely. The FDA notice did not report any illnesses or injuries linked to the recalled toothpaste.

Many of the affected tubes were marketed to kids. The recalled products include toothpaste sold under the Brush Buddies, Crayola, Hot Wheels and My Little Pony brands, in flavors such as bubble gum, strawberry, watermelon, peppermint, sweet mint and cool mint. They were distributed by Ashtel Studios Inc. of Ontario, California, and come in 3.5-ounce and 4-ounce tubes, plus a two-pack of 3.5-ounce tubes.

Affected products carry expiration dates from November 2026 through June 2028, and consumers should check the lot numbers and expiration dates on the FDA’s recall notice to see whether theirs is included.
What to do if you have the recalled toothpaste

The FDA’s recall notice doesn’t include specific instructions for consumers, and neither the manufacturer nor the distributor has issued public guidance on returns or refunds. Until they do, the safest move is to stop using the toothpaste immediately and toss it out. Start by checking the brand, lot number and expiration date on your tube against the FDA’s recall notice; if it matches, discard it and switch to a different fluoride toothpaste so your family’s brushing routine isn’t interrupted.

Hang on to your receipt or take a photo of the packaging before tossing it, in case a refund process is announced later. No illnesses or injuries have been reported, but if you or your child used the product and have any concerns, you should contact your dentist or doctor immediately.
Other toothpastes to use instead
The below toothpastes were not recalled and have at least a four-star average rating from thousands of customers.
Tom's of Maine Natural Kids Fluoride Toothpaste

My kids absolutely love this toothpaste — in fact, it is the only one they will use. The fruity flavor makes brushing less of a chore, while fluoride fights cavities and calcium and silica gently clean teeth. It’s approved by the American Dental Association (ADA), free of artificial colors, flavors, and preservatives, and suitable for children ages 2 and up.
Crest Kid’s Cavity Protection Toothpaste

This toothpaste’s bright blue, sparkly color will delight kids. Plus, the fluoride formula fights cavities while staying gentle on enamel, and it carries the ADA Seal of Acceptance. It is suitable for children ages 2 and up, with adult supervision.

If you can’t decide on which hello kids’ flavor your little one will love, grab this variety pack that lets them sample all three and pick a favorite. Each toothpaste comes in a brightly colored tube with an easy flip cap that sits flat when closed, so it stands neatly on the bathroom counter.
Crest Pro-Health Advanced Antibacterial Protection Toothpaste, 4-Pack

If you had one of the adult toothpastes in the recall, Crest Pro-Health Advanced is a reliable replacement from a brand you already know. It’s an antibacterial fluoride toothpaste that fights plaque bacteria and supports healthy gums. It also helps whiten teeth and strengthen enamel.

story: A man was arrested Friday night near the Brooklyn set of “Miami Vice ’85,” a film starring Michael B. Jordan and Austin Butler.

Alex Perez, 23, of Brooklyn, was arrested just after 11 p.m. on accusations that he displayed a knife during a verbal dispute with another man in the area of Avenue N and McDonald Avenue, the New York City Police Department said.
“The individual was then taken into custody without incident, and the knife was recovered,” the NYPD said.
For Subscribers
No one was injured.
