title: Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders take legal action against My Chemical Romance over onstage costumes
summary: The parent company of the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders is taking legal action against My Chemical Romance after the band performed alongside dancers in costumes resembling the iconic cheerleading team’s uniforms this week.
story: The parent company of the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders is taking legal action against My Chemical Romance after the band performed alongside dancers in costumes resembling the iconic cheerleading team’s uniforms this week.

Pro Silver Star, which owns the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders brand, filed a motion for a temporary restraining order and preliminary injunction Friday in district court in Dallas County, Texas, seeking to bar the alternative rock band from using the costumes onstage.

My Chemical Romance, best known for its 2000s hits “Teenagers” and “Welcome to the Black Parade,” performed Wednesday at the Hollywood Bowl in Los Angeles with dancers wearing outfits that appeared nearly identical to the squad’s iconic white and blue uniforms, according to the court filing.
The dancers carried what appeared to be rifles and engaged in a staged firefight, “only to be depicted being shot,” the filing states.

“Audience members and online commentators understandably believed that the performers were the real Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders and said so in social media posts that continue to circulate,” Pro Silver Star wrote.
The company said it was “not litigious” and “takes no issue with MCR’s music, its artistic ambitions, or any message Defendants seek to convey.”
For Subscribers
“Silver Star asks only that those performers not wear the DCC Uniform while doing it,” the filing states. “The universe of alternative costume designs is effectively unlimited.”
For Subscribers
Representatives for the band and Pro Silver Star did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

My Chemical Romance is on tour celebrating the 20th anniversary of its third studio album, “The Black Parade.” The band is scheduled to perform at the Hollywood Bowl again on Saturday evening and twice over Halloween weekend.

title: ‘An unfortunate mistake’: Knicks admit error in using championship rings as phishing bait
summary: The New York Knicks’ parent company says it is giving out more than $3.7 million worth of championship rings and jewelry after acknowledging an “unfortunate mistake” of using an offer of free rings to lure employees into a cybersecurity test. As first reported by The Athletic, the email said employees were eligible for a free Knicks championship ring.
story: The New York Knicks’ parent company says it is giving out more than $3.7 million worth of championship rings and jewelry after acknowledging an “unfortunate mistake” of using an offer of free rings to lure employees into a cybersecurity test.

As first reported by The Athletic, the email said employees were eligible for a free Knicks championship ring. Instead, clicking on the offer earned them a mandatory cybersecurity training, the outlet reported.

“The company had previously sent out an email to its corporate team as a simulation of a phishing attack designed to strengthen our security against hackers,” Madison Square Garden Sports said in a statement. “MSG was recently hacked and extorted using an employee login and password obtained through a similar phishing attack.”
For Subscribers
The company said it is giving players, coaches, employees and others in the Knicks organization more than 275 rings and pieces of jewelry worth more than $3.7 million.
For Subscribers

NFL Network host Rich Eisen criticized Knicks owner James L. Dolan over the email on his show, saying: “The man is phishing his own employees with a bait of a championship ring. Can you be any worse of an employer? Can you be any lower than that?”

The Athletic also reported that Knicks assistant coaches were handed empty boxes during the ring ceremony ahead of the Knicks’ first game of the season on Tuesday. The assistants had been told earlier that day they would not receive their rings that evening but would get them eventually, according to the outlet.

title: 12 injured, including several minors, in shooting near Florida A&M University stadium
summary: Twelve people, including several minors, were injured in a shooting near Florida A&M University’s Bragg Memorial Stadium, where homecoming celebrations included a football game Saturday.
story: Twelve people, including several minors, were injured in a shooting near Florida A&M University’s Bragg Memorial Stadium, where homecoming celebrations included a football game Saturday.

The Tallahassee Police Department said in a statement that 11 of the 12 were shot and that three victims had serious injuries, with one minor in serious condition. The others, it said, were in stable condition.
Six of the injured are under 18 years old and the youngest is 11 years old, Chief Lawrence Revell of the Tallahassee Police Department said at a press conference early Sunday morning.
“Our preliminary information shows that an altercation occurred between individuals,” he added, describing it as “an isolated incident between two or three individuals.”
Revell said that no arrests had yet been made, nor anyone taken into custody, but that police believed one shooter was involved.
“Our priority is to determine what happened and why it happened, and to bring the people that are responsible for this to justice,” he added, asking any witnesses to come forward.

The violence unfolded about 8 p.m. at an intersection adjacent to Bragg Memorial Stadium, it said. Early in the evening, Florida A&M’s Rattlers hosted the Arkansas-Pine Bluff Golden Lions for the historically Black university’s annual homecoming game.
After the shooting took place, the university issued a statement on X asking members of its campus community to stay away from the area.
It described the shooting as having taken place “near campus,” which it said was safe.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
“Our hearts are with the victims and everyone affected by tonight’s incident on Perry Street,” the university said.
Florida State University, about a mile away from Florida A&M, issued an emergency alert about the violence and said it didn’t appear anyone from its school community was involved.
“As a precaution, students, faculty and staff in the Tallahassee area are advised to remain indoors this evening and stay alert,” it said.

Revell offered condolences to the victims and their families, and also praised officers who he said ran without hesitation “into the middle of this, still not knowing where the shooters were, still not knowing how many victims we had.”
“We had officers that were picking up victims and carrying them in their arms to transport victims because they couldn’t get through the mass of people,” he said.
The investigation into the violence was ongoing, and police asked witnesses to come forward.

title: Paris Hilton Recreates Iconic Britney Spears VMAs Outfit For Halloween, Live Snake and All.
summary: For Halloween, Paris Hilton recreated the pop princess Britney Spears’ legendary look from her 2001 performance at the MTV Video Music Awards.
story: Socialite and businesswoman Paris Hilton’s Halloween costume is totally #Sliving.

Hilton recreated the pop princess Britney Spears’ legendary look from her 2001 performance at the MTV Video Music Awards. And the reality star, who revealed the costume on Oct. 23, simply nailed the ensemble — down to the live yellow snake.

“I always had the utmost respect for Brittany, but the fact that she performed at the VMAs with one of these around her neck is the most legendary thing that I’ve ever heard of my life,” Hilton said in a behind-the-scenes video shared on Instagram. “Especially after experiencing it just in the hallway of my house, I can’t imagine being on stage performing in front of thousands of people with this around my shoulders. That is badass. I love you, Brit.”

To recreate the look, Hilton rocked a green top, disco shorts that featured a blue and green ombré butterfly print and a bedazzled belt with shimmering, rhinestone tassels. She also posed with a snake named Tango around her neck, just as the daring pop star did during that iconic 2001 performance of “I’m a Slave 4 U.” In the behind-the-scenes video, Tango’s handler shared that the snake weighs roughly 30-40 lbs.
Now, that’s commitment.
Spears’ VMAs performance at New York City’s Metropolitan Opera house has become the stuff of legend in the two decades that have passed since she famously donned a yellow snake around her neck.

During the act, Spears, then 19, begins the routine inside a cage with a live tiger. Wearing a costume created by designers Kurt Swanson and Bart Mueller, Spears, giving some real jungle vibes, performs the striking act before ending it with Banana, the python.

Since, the performance has been praised as one of the most memorable moments in the VMAs’ over 40-year history. And plenty of people have referenced Spears’ daring act. In 2001, actor Elle Fanning also recreated the look for Halloween.
Actor Elle Fanning recreated the look as well for Halloween in 2021. She pulled it off flawlessly — even if the snake was fake.

title: Janet Jackson Makes Rare Public Appearance In An Outfit That’s ‘Nasty’ In The Best Way
summary: Pop icon Janet Jackson, 60, stepped out for a rare public appearance at the Dancers Against Cancer’s Gala of the Stars on Oct. 22 in Beverly Hills. Jackson, who presented an award to rapper Missy Elliott later on in the night, shut down the red carpet with her absolutely nasty look.
story: Ms. Jackson has entered the building.

Pop icon Janet Jackson, 60, stepped out for a rare public appearance at Dancers Against Cancer’s Gala of the Stars on Oct. 22 in Beverly Hills. Jackson, who presented an award to rapper Missy Elliott later on in the night, shut down the red carpet with her absolutely nasty look.
“Janet is ageless! That dress is stunning!” one social media user wrote on platform Threads.
Jackson’s ensemble featured a black lace, custom Christian Siriano gown. The dress included long sleeves and a peplum skirt around the hips. She completed the look with an elegant slicked-back ‘do.
The look received praise across the internet, including from a couple of style icons in their own right.
“Major,” celebrity stylist Law Roach commented under a photo of the pop god.

Jackson’s appearance was part of a star-studded event that aimed to raise funds to help support dancers, choreographers and their families amid battles with cancer. The event, hosted by “Dancing With The Stars” alum Maksim Chmerkovskiy, honored a number of big names in dance, including Toni Basil, Hilaria Baldwin, Vincent Paterson and the late Chita Rivera.

Jackson introduced honoree Missy Elliott before presenting the “Work It” rapper with the Icon Award. In her heartfelt speech, Jackson described the rapper, who’s long been known for imaginative dance routines in music videos and performances, as someone who “elevated choreography, embraced individuality, and inspired generations of dancers to dream bigger.”

“That influence lives far beyond a single song or a single performance,” Jackson said in the speech, which received tremendous applause. “It lives in every artist who feels a little braver because Missy showed them what was possible.”
Elliott later shared a heartfelt post about her friend Jackson.

“Dear @janetjackson we have been friends way over two decades, & I still am one of your BIGGEST fans! Of course, I’m a fan of your music, BUT I’m the biggest fan of YOU, the PERSON!” Elliott wrote in the emotional Instagram post. “With all that you’ve done globally, you have NEVER been loudest in the room, but those in the room know you are MOTHA! Your SELFLESSNESS & HUMILITY should be studied! Your beauty outside matches the INSIDE!”
Elliott concluded by expressing her love for Jackson.
“I Love you, j, & thank you for this award it’s the best feeling getting a ICON award from a ICON!” she wrote.

title: Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders Take Legal Action Against Band My Chemical Romance
summary: The parent company of the famed cheerleading squad the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders have filed a temporary restraining order against popular rock band My Chemical Romance over a costume dispute.
story: The parent company of the famed cheerleading squad the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders have filed a temporary restraining order against popular rock band My Chemical Romance over a costume dispute.

Pro Silver Star, the owner of the high-profile cheerleading squad’s brand, filed a motion Oct. 23, seeking a temporary restraining order to bar the “Welcome to the Black Parade” band from using the squad’s iconic costumes on stage.

It comes after the band’s recent performances at the Hollywood Bowl in Los Angeles featured dancers in what appeared to be Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders-inspired outfits. In their court filing, Pro Silver Star argued that the use of the outfits weren’t authorized.

In the legal filing, the company said that it takes “no issue” with the band’s music, nor is it looking for the defendants to change their choreography or “even their decision to put gun-toting performers on stage.”
“Silver Star asks only that those performers not wear the DCC Uniform while doing it,” the company said in the filing. “The universe of alternative costume designs is effectively unlimited.”
My Chemical Romance did not immediately respond to TODAY.com’s request for comment.
Pro Silver Star is also seeking a preliminary injunction on the use of the costumes, according to the motion that was filed in the District Court of Dallas County.

In the document, Pro Silver Star alleges that during the band’s opening night at the Hollywood Bowl on Oct. 21, the rock group had a line of female dancers, dressed as the DCC cheerleaders, to perform a choreographed routine during the hit song “Teenagers.” The “counterfeit uniforms” reflected the “signature elements” of the DCC outfit, from the white boots to the white vest with blue stars.
Fan videos from the night show the performers, holding blue-and-white pom-poms, dancing in unison to the hit 2006 single.
The filing then says that the costumed performers were handed rifles and joined in a staged firefight before then “depicted being shot and crawling off the stage.”

“The brand DCC built on dedication, character, and community, and on decades of entertaining American troops, was thus put on a stage in a gunfight, its uniform worn by performers shown shooting and being shot,” the filing said.

My Chemical Romance has long been a staple in the alt rock scene and counter culture movements. Climbing the charts in the 2000s with emo hits like “Helena” the band hit the peak of its commercial success with 2006 album “The Black Parade.” The band’s shows at the Hollywood Bowl are part of a 20th anniversary tour in celebration of the album. The band will perform again at the iconic venue on Oct. 24.

title: Prince William Reveals He Went Through a DJ Phase — and Even Had A Stage Name
summary: Prince William, who joined the Oct. 23 episode of “The Graham Norton Show,” opened up about how he once aspired to be a DJ in his younger years. And he even had a stage name.
story: Prince William could’ve been the king of the club.
The 44-year-old royal, who joined the Oct. 23 episode of “The Graham Norton Show,” opened up about how he once aspired to be a DJ in his younger years. And he even had a stage name.
“I went through a phase where I wanted to be a DJ, which didn’t go very well,” the prince said, laughing. “And I came up with a name. It was called DJ Xara with an X. It wasn’t good.”

William — who joined the longtime British talk show alongside fellow guests Cate Blanchett, Hannah Waddingham and Robert Irwin — acknowledged that as a child, he did, in fact, fantasize about going into a non-royal profession.
William told host Graham Norton that at one point, he thought about perhaps becoming a police officer.
“Being a policeman, I thought was quite cool,” William said.
Then came the DJ phase, William explained. Unfortunately, the Prince of Wales never got to play any gigs. When asked if he ever DJ’d any school parties, the prince gave an honest answer.
“No, I didn’t,” William said, smiling. “I never got that good.”

Prince William, the heir apparent to the British throne, may not be in the DJ booth these days, but he appears to be pretty busy, working on charitable projects and carrying out his official royal duties. Some of his main causes include the environment, homelessness and the armed forces.

He does, of course, have down time, which he fills with some good ‘ol reality TV. Prince William told Norton that he and his children are big fans of “The Celebrity Traitors,” hosted by broadcaster Claudia Winkleman.
“I love it. The family love it,” he said of the show. “Charlotte and Louis are obsessed with it. It’s really good telly.”

title: Alfonso Ribeiro Shares Why He Was Nervous to Dance With Tatyana Ali on ‘Dancing With the Stars’
summary: Alfonso Ribeiro tells TODAY.com about how he felt nervous to perform with Tatyana Ali during “Dancing With the Stars” Dedication Night.
story: Dedication Night on “Dancing With the Stars” is the episode that pulls at the heartstrings, and this year was no different. It was also the night that made co-host Alfonso Ribeiro the most “nervous.”

During the Oct. 20 episode, Tatyana Ali honored the late James Avery. The “Fresh Prince of Bel-Air” star and partner Jan Ravnik danced a Viennese waltz to “(You Don’t Know) How Glad I Am” by Nancy Wilson.
Already an emotional number, it became extra heartwarming when Ali was joined by Ribeiro, who stepped in midway and replaced Ravnik.

“It was nice. It was the first time I’ve actually felt nervous. Even my whole season, I never felt nervous,” Ribeiro, who won Season 19 of “DWTS,” tells TODAY.com. “But I was nervous because I wanted to be great for her, for James Avery. It wasn’t about me.”

Ali and Ribeiro worked alongside Avery for six seasons of the sitcom from 1990 to 1996. They portrayed siblings, Ashley and Carlton Banks, while Avery was the ever-wise, stern, yet softie dad Philip Banks. Avery died Dec. 31, 2013 at the age of 68.
For the performance, Ali waltzed around the ballroom floor with Ravnik before she and Ribeiro continued the routine in synchronized steps.
At the conclusion of the tribute, they held hands and a photo of a smiling Avery appeared on the screen. They turned to face their former TV dad, before embracing.
Ribeiro says he wanted to make the moment great for Ali, which meant making sure he didn’t miss a beat.

“When I was competing on the show ... if I mess up, I cause harm to myself ... but I had to lead Tatyana,” he says. “I had to be the one during that part of the routine where I’m taking the place of Jan and I’m actually having to lead in that dance — a dance that I never did before.”

Ribeiro, who won with pro Witney Carson, says he never tackled the Viennese waltz. Despite the additional challenge, he says, “It was so wonderful to be a part of that. I felt incredibly honored to be asked to be a part of their number and to represent James Avery.”
He notes that as co-host of “DWTS,” he takes “being neutral to all of the contestants very seriously.” However, he didn’t want to pass up this opportunity.

“But this was special because it was James Avery. James played my dad on three different sitcoms,” he says, referring to 1995’s “In the House” and the short-lived “Things We Do for Love.” “It was very special to be able to do that for him, and it was nice to be able to collaborate with Jan and with Tatyana on what the story was going to be, and it was beautiful.”
The “America’s Funniest Home Videos” host also noted that Ross Bagley, who played Nicky Banks on “Fresh Prince,” was in attendance that night, as well.
When asked if he and Ali had heard from Avery’s family following the dedication, he says yes.
“There was a text chain with all of us, and basically everyone was like, ‘Beautifully said. Beautifully done. James would be very proud,’” he shares. “So it felt good.”

title: Prince William Shares the Reality Show Princess Charlotte and Prince Louis Are ‘Obsessed With’
summary: Prince William revealed that a reality television show that has quickly become a global phenomenon has also captured the attention of Princess Charlotte and Prince Louis.
story: Prince William has revealed that a reality television show that has quickly become a global phenomenon has also captured the attention of the royal family.

The Prince of Wales made a surprise appearance on Britain’s “The Graham Norton Show” Oct. 23 and opened up about some of his favorite pastimes. While sitting on the couch next to fellow celebrity guests Cate Blanchett, Hannah Waddingham and Robert Irwin, Prince William told host Graham Norton that his family are big fans of “The Celebrity Traitors.”
“I love it. The family love it. Charlotte and Louis are obsessed with it. It’s really good telly,” he praised.
U.K. series “Celebrity Traitors,” hosted by Claudia Winkleman, began airing its second season on Oct. 1. Prince William said he recently tried to re-create a moment from the season premiere.

“I saw Ross Kemp the day after the first episode and I couldn’t help but try — in the most appropriate way – to touch him to see what reaction I got from him. Turns out he was really jumpy!” he marveled.

Kemp, a reporter, went viral after the first episode for his paranoia. He wondered if singer and Little Mix star Leigh-Anne Pinnock might be a Traitor after she lightly tapped his shoulder while walking around the castle.
In addition to Pinnock and Kemp, the cast this season also features Richard E. Grant, Michael Sheen and Miranda Hart.
During his time on “The Graham Norton Show,” Prince William shared other ways he likes to unwind.
“It is music and film. I love getting immersed in deep-thinking films. I like action films too, but I like something a bit different,” he said.
The British royal revealed he is a huge fan of Christopher Nolan.

“His films are fantastic — ‘The Dark Knight’ series is psychologically dark and deep and I absolutely love that. He takes concepts that are completely out there and makes them incredibly entertaining,” he gushed.
The royal family supports some of their favorite Hollywood stars from time to time at public events.
In September, the prince and his wife, Catherine, Princess of Wales, attended the world premiere of “Digger” in London. They were photographed chatting with star Tom Cruise on the red carpet.

How ‘ACOTAR’ and ‘Throne of Glass’ Connect
The first explicit crossover between Maas’ series came in 2018, with the “Throne of Glass” finale, “Kingdom of Ash.”

As Aelin falls between worlds at the peak of her battle with the Valg, she passes through a “world of snowcapped mountains under shining stars” and sees two Fae: one winged male and one “heavily pregnant female.” The male notices her falling and sends his power, “like a gentle summer night,” to slow her down. This is Rhysand and Feyre, likely during the events of “A Court of Silver Flames,” which lines up with her pregnancy.

When “A Court of Silver Flames” published in 2021, some readers believed that moment was seen from the other perspective. In Chapter 62, after the annual Starfall event, a “rare red star” is spotted blasting across the sky and is interpreted as an “ill omen.”
How ‘ACOTAR’ and ‘Crescent City’ Connect
“Crescent City” more clearly establishes that the worlds of Maas’ three series are interconnected, starting with last line of the last chapter in Book 2, “House of Sky and Breath.”

At the end of “Crescent City” 2, heroine Bryce Quinlan confronts the Asteri, the rulers of her planet, Midgard. She learns they are not benevolent leaders but parasites who survive on firstlight generated by magical beings. When she learns the truth, she tries to use the Horn, which can open rifts between worlds, to go to Hel for help against the Asteri.

Instead she lands in another world, surrounded by Fae who believe her to be a threat. One of them looks eerily similar to her brother, Ruhn. When Bryce says her name, that Fae male responds: “Hello, Bryce Quinlan. My name is Rhysand.”
And there ends Book 2.

Book 3, “House of Flame and Shadow,” picks up where Book 2 leaves off. When Bryce lands in Prythian, Rhys and his Inner Circle interrogate Bryce. Soon they all learn that the Asteri, the primary villains in “Crescent City,” are the same as the Daglan, an evil force found in the history books of Prythian.

Readers learn in “A Court of Silver Flames” that the Daglan were vanquished by Rhys’ ancestors 15,000 years before the events of the books. But in “House of Flame and Shadow,” Bryce discovers that the Daglan escaped to Midgard to conquer a new planet and curate sources of power to serve as food. But they have maintained a desire to find a way back to their home world.

The ancient Fae relic known as the Horn is a big part of “Crescent City” lore. It’s first introduced in “House of Earth and Blood” when it goes missing from its place in Luna’s Temple. By the end of the book, readers learn Bryce’s best friend, Danika, had discovered the Horn’s ability to open doors between worlds, ground it into ashes, mixed it with ink and imbued it onto Bryce’s back as a tattoo when she was drunk. This was Danika’s effort to hide the Horn from the evil people looking for it and happened days before she was killed.

While Bryce is in Prythian in “House of Flame and Shadow,” she learns that the Horn is actually part of the Dread Trove, a collection of powerful artifacts made by the Cauldron. In a “Court of Silver Flames,” Nesta and the Night Court find the other three relics in the Trove — the Harp, the Crown and the Mask.

And speaking of missing artifacts — Bryce and the Night Court crew also learn in “House of Flame and Shadow” that Gwydion, a long-missing sword that’s a pair to spymaster Azriel’s dagger Truth-Teller, is none other than Bryce’s Starsword, a weapon in Midgard that can only be wielded by the chosen Starborn Fae.

In “House of Flame and Shadow,” Bryce at first tries to hide from the Night Court crew her tattoo that contains the Horn. The tattoo is written in a script Bryce doesn’t even know and is supposed to translate to, “Through love, all is possible.”

Amren is first to clock the tattoo and tells Rhys that Bryce’s tattoo is written in the same language found in “The Book of Breathings,” an object in the “ACOTAR” world with an ability to control the Cauldron. The book is also mysteriously mentioned in “House of Earth and Blood”; it’s in Jesiba Roga’s library alongside “The Walking Dead,” a book from “Throne of Glass.”

In “A Court of Mist and Fury,” Amren identifies the language in which “The Book of Breathings” is written as “Leshon Kadoesh” or “The Holy Tongue.” Rhys then shares that, according to legend, the language is one “of mighty beings who were here ... and then vanished.”

In “House of Flame and Shadow,” Bryce teams up with Nesta and Azriel to navigate a tunnel system near the Prison, led by the light from the glowing eight-pointed star on Bryce’s chest. One of the obstacles they face is the Middengard Wyrm, a large-toothed monster that Feyre faces in the first “ACOTAR” book.
But Bryce raises an interesting question when facing the creature.
“Middengard? Like — Midgard? Did they come from my world originally?” she asks, though Nesta and Azriel are unable to answer.

The theory of a lost Dusk Court was popular among “ACOTAR” fans, since it felt like a glaring omission from Prythian’s landscape. The continent has four seasonal courts — Spring, Autumn, Summer and Winter — and three solar courts — Night, Day and Dawn, but no Dusk.
It turns, it did once exist.

In “House of Flame and Shadow,” Bryce, Azriel and Nesta end up in the Prison via the tunnel system and find the same spot Nesta had found the Harp in “A Court of Silver Flames.” (The Harp was notably found on top of a “large rendering of an eight-pointed star.”) (Notably, Nesta has an eight-pointed star on her spine, and Bryce has one that glows on her chest.) (Also notably, a High Priestess in “Throne of Glass” has an eight-pointed star tattooed on her forehead.)

The three then encounter a hologram of Silene, the long lost daughter of Theia, a Fae queen and the original Starborn. Though Bryce already knew she is a descendent of Theia, Silene’s storytelling is how she learns that the Starborn Fae of Midgard had originated in Prythian.

According to Silene, Theia had served the Daglan for a long time while in Prythian, but eventually overthrew them and was able to claim her land — the island on which the Prison is located — for herself. That land thrived with “dusk, twilight — that’s what the island was in its long-buried heart.”

But after getting greedy for power, Theia and her court — as well as people with red hair who “looked alarmingly like Bryce’s father,” the Autumn King — migrated to Midgard, only to find themselves trapped under the reign of the very creatures they had fought to overthrow.

Silene was able to return to Prythian and escape the Asteri, but she concealed her power and the memory of ancestors vanished. The land of the former Dusk Court around her died, forming the barren isolation of the Prison. When Silene eventually married her mate, a High Lord of the Night Court, her firstborn son glowed with starlight inherited from her. “It was light of the evening star. The dusk star,” she says.
Bryce’s Starborn power is later described as a “dusk power,” a force the princes of Hel also call “starfire.”
How ‘Crescent City’ Connects to ‘Throne of Glass’

“House of Flame and Shadow” contains notable crossovers with “Throne of Glass,” Maas’ first series published in 2012. But many speculate that the world of “Crescent City” was first alluded to in “Kingdom of Ash,” the last book in the “Throne of Glass” series.

When Aelin falls between worlds — in the same instance she passes by Rhys and Feyre, as mentioned above — she also passes by a “world where a great city had been built along the curve of a river, the buildings impossibly tall and glimmering with lights.” It’s likely this is Lunathion, aka the titular Crescent City, which gets its name from the bend of the Istros River through it.
From there, though, most connections are seen in passing references and winks at the series.

The most overt connection between “Crescent City” and “Throne of Glass” comes in “House of Flame and Shadow” with the Under-King’s passing reference to Wyrd, which he describes as his home planet’s equivalent of Midgard’s Urd, the goddess of fate.

Wyrd, however, isn’t a goddess, but a “force that governed worlds. A cauldron of life, brimming with the language of creation,” says Under-King, the head of Lunathion’s Bone Quarter and leader of the House of Flame and Shadow.

In “Throne of Glass,” Wyrd, pronounced “word,” is indeed everywhere. The central conflict across the eight-book series centers on Aelin’s attempts to close the Wyrdgates, essentially portals between worlds (sound familiar?) by gathering all the Wyrdkeys. Her goal is to destroy the keys to prevent the Valg, demons that possess people and feed off their souls (again, sound familiar?), from coming to her world and conquering it with the power of Wyrdstone. She also learns to harness the power of Wyrdmarks, aka, magic runes.

It’s unclear if the Valg of “Throne of Glass” are the same as the Asteri/Dalgan, though both beings aim to conquer and consume. But “House of Flame and Shadow” does contain several references to the Asteri’s power over worlds as a “collar,” which is a major tool the Valg used to possess people, like Dorian.
After “House of Sky and Breath,” readers learned that shifters, including wolves like Ithan and Danika, are also Fae who just originated from a different world.

Once Ithan takes Hypaxia’s antidote to the Asteri’s power blocker in “House of Flame and Shadow,” he learns that his power wasn’t always just limited to shifting. He also has the power of wielding snow and ice.

The combination of an animal form and an elemental power is the prototype of the Fae found in “Throne of Glass,” suggesting shifters like Ithan came from the same world as Aelin. Fans of that series will remember Rowan Whitethorn could shift into a hawk and could wield wind.

Let’s also go back to the tale told by Silene, the daughter Queen Theia. When recounting to Bryce, Nesta and Azriel how Theia led a takeover of Midgard, she notes that the rifts opened once again and more Fae appeared “from another world this time.”

“They were Fae like us, but not,” Silene says. “The ears, the grace, the strength were identical, but they were shape-shifters, all of them. Each capable of turning into an animal. And each, even in their humanoid body, equipped with elongated canine teeth.”
Ithan, armed with his newly discovered powers, later takes on the Under-King directly.
The Under-King reveals that he, too, came from the same world as the shifters, the world of “Throne of Glass.” Before Midgard, he was confined to “caves and barrows,” he says.
After the Under-King interrupts Ithan’s final meeting with Connor, the wolf’s rage is heightened by his new Fae powers, and his blood “sings” that the creature is an “enemy.”
“It spoke of caves beneath hills, of plundered graves and musty darkness. Enemy,” Ithan thinks, before destroying the Under-King with the help of Hypaxia.

The Under-King is likely related to a barrow-wight from “Heir of Fire,” the third “Throne of Glass” book. A barrow-wight is a creature that infests tombs, coveting treasure. Aelin faces them while training with Rowan in Mistward.
Lidia Cervos, aka the Hind, undergoes a 360-degree transformation from the first “Crescent City” book to the third. The ruthless deer shifter turns out to be a rebel, a mom and mate to Ruhn.

As a shifter, she comes from the world of “Throne of Glass,” like Ithan. But the connection doesn’t stop there. Lidia turns out to have fire in her veins from an “old bloodline” on her father’s side — and that fire becomes “a song in her blood” in the fight against the Asteri.

She explains that the fire comes from her family’s legend of Brannon, “a Fae King from another world, fire in his veins, who had created stags with the power of flame to be his sacred guards.” It’s why she named her son Brannon, Brann for short.

Lidia is likely a descendant of Brannon Galathynius, a major player in the lore of “Throne of Glass.” Brannon is the founder of Terrasen and an ancestor of Aelin Galathynius, who also has the power of fire.

Another potential connection to Aelin is more subtle — Lidia’s ruby ring. Lidia eventually gives this ring to her sons, dismissing it as “an heirloom of my father’s household. He’s not anyone worth remembering.”

But that ring might be one Aelin and Rowan discover in “Kingdom of Ash” from a barrow-wight’s mound of pilfered treasure. Among the gold, they find a pair of rings, one an “elegantly cut ruby within the band itself,” and the other, “a sparkling rectangular emerald.” The pair exchange the rings, Aelin receiving the emerald and Rowan the ruby, in a impromptu ceremony, vowing they’ll stay together “to whatever end.”

Other subtle connections to Aelin and Terrasen, her kingdom in “Throne of Glass,” include the constant stag imagery through the Fae kingdom of Avallen. Terrasen is known as the home of the sun stags, put there by Brannon, and the land is blessed the Lord of the North, a great stag with flaming antlers. Similarly, Avallen’s leader, Morven, is described as the Stag King, with a throne made “from the bones of some noble, butchered beast.”

But the most overt reference that many Maas fans pointed to when the name of the third “Crescent City” book was announced did not come to fruition. Aelin, who is referred to, among many titles, as the Queen of Flame and Shadow once in the “Throne of Glass” series, does not make an appearance in “House of Flame and Shadow.”

Hypaxia, the witch-queen, takes the Under-King’s place as the leader of the shadowy faction by the end of the book. However, she is always referred to as the Head of the House of Flame and Shadow — never the queen.

title: Christina Ricci Shares Why She Rarely Celebrated Halloween and What Changed
summary: Christina Ricci shares her past Halloween memories and how she has a newfound appreciate for the holiday thanks to her children.
story: Christina Ricci’s favorite holiday is Christmas.
It’s an unexpected answer from the actor, whose credits include Halloween classics “The Addams Family,” “Casper” and “Sleepy Hollow.”

“I don’t look at things from the outside. So for me, I’ve been a part of like three movies that are supernaturally themed and some of them have been held up to be very iconic,” Ricci, 46, tells TODAY.com, adding that she knows people associate her with the spooky season. “But my favorite holiday is Christmas.”
As a kid, she says, she would often be working on Halloween so she didn’t do much trick-or-treating. “I did a little bit, and certainly when I was really small I would go with my family,” Ricci adds.
The “Yellowjackets” star, however, says she’s grown to appreciate the holiday and the “enthusiasm with which people attack Halloween.”
“I love when people go really big. I love when people have the giant spiders coming over the garage or the huge animatronic skeletons,” she says.
She recently started to get even more into the Halloween spirit thanks to her children; 12 year-old son Freddie and 4-year-old daughter Cleopatra.
“Halloween has been a thing ever since I had my own kids,” she says. “So now I do Halloween because of my kids and I’ve really learned to appreciate it.”

This year, she especially leaned into the holiday when she teamed up with “Hocus Pocus” icon Kathy Najimy, as well as creators Rachel Iwanyszyn, Zaire Alford and Macy Blackwell, to create a council and decide the winner of Reese’s Trick-or-Treatiest Street in America. East Dudley Avenue in Westfield, New Jersey, was crowned the champion.
Ricci says it was nice to celebrate creativity, individuality and community, sharing how it was wonderful to see “neighborhoods and people coming together.”

Ricci — whose “favorite candy of all time is Reese’s Pieces” — will also partake in her own festivities with her neighbors. She adds that this year is extra special because her daughter will experience a Halloween first.
“This year will be the first year that my 4 year old, she’s almost five, will probably do a little bit of street trick-or-treating,” she says. “And that should be fun.”
She shares that she’ll take her kids around their neighborhood before one of the families hosts a big chili cookout at night after the trick-or-treating is over.
While she notes that she does not dress up for Halloween, her children already have their costumes picked out.

“But I will say when I was a child, I’m the youngest of four kids, my mom had this gorilla costume that all the kids wore,” she says. “And then I was able to wear it for like four years in a row, so I would just always be a gorilla in costume.”
One year, she was a gorilla ballerina and another time she was a gorilla teenager, she says. “That is the only recurring costume that I have in my past.”

title: Constance Wu Shares New Details About ‘Crazy Rich Asians’ TV Show Sequel
summary: Constance Wu starred in the 2018 blockbuster rom-com “Crazy Rich Asians” and shared some details about the long-awaited follow-up to the film.
story: The upcoming “Crazy Rich Asians” sequel sounds like it’s going to be an insane amount of fun, according to actor Constance Wu.
Wu, who starred in the 2018 blockbuster rom-com, stopped by TODAY on Oct. 23 and shared some details about the long-awaited follow-up to the film, an HBO series.
The actor, who said she’s seen the script, had some high-praise for the highly-anticipated project. The TV show, written by the movie’s co-writer Adele Lim, will feature original cast members.

“I love it, it’s very funny,” Wu told co-hosts Laura Jarrett, Dylan Dreyer and Craig Melvin. “I think it’s really good. We’re in great hands because Adele is show-running and writing, and she did the original, and she’s just so smart and good and talented that I feel just great being with her sort of at the helm.”

For years, fans have been asking for a sequel to the smash hit film. And after almost a decade since the original movie was released, HBO announced earlier this month that a sequel had officially been greenlit.

This time around, it’ll be an eight-episode series that draws from the world of Kevin Kwan’s bestselling “Crazy Rich Asians” trilogy. Already, its biggest stars — Wu along with Henry Golding, Ronny Chieng and Michelle Yeoh — have been confirmed to reprise their roles.
“I can tell you that we’re all excited to be coming back,” Wu said.

The actor, who’s currently promoting Prime Video thriller series “The Terminal List” also shared that the “Crazy Rich Asians” sequel, is slated to begin filming next year in New York, where she lives.

While fans have loved the original film for its extreme displays of opulence and wealth, in addition to the juicy drama, many have also upheld the rom-com as a major turning point for Asian American representation. It marked a rare moment in which mainstream audiences could see an all-Asian cast on the big screen.

title: Queen Camilla, Winnie-the-Pooh and the Rumor that Caused the British Embassy to Speak Up
summary: A breakdown of the possible feud that could be brewing between Queen Camilla and the New York Public Library over where Winnie-the-Pooh belongs.
story: “Catch Me Up” is a TODAY series where our experts and journalists bring readers up to speed on the day’s biggest headlines.
A decades-old debate over where the original Winnie-the-Pooh should reside has reached the point where even the British embassy is weighing in.
The embassy released a statement denying reports that the United Kingdom wants the iconic stuffed bear to return back to England.

This year marks the 100th birthday of “Winnie-the-Pooh,” the children’s classic that was penned by A.A. Milne and first published on Oct. 14, 1926. The anniversary has come with speculation over where the stuffed version of the lovable bear should be kept.

It’s currently on display at the New York Public Library, where it has been sitting in a glass case for millions to see since 1987. The owner of the dolls donated them to the library 39 years ago, according to the NYPL.

Gyles Brandreth, an author and friend of Milne’s son Christopher, told The Washington Post that he traveled to the New York Public Library in 2024 as an emissary of Queen Camilla hoping to arrange Pooh and friends’ temporary return to Buckingham Palace in London for the 100th anniversary of the book, but his request was denied by library officials.
The article ignited a response from New York City and library officials, followed by a reply from the British Embassy.

Here’s what to know about the drama involving Queen Camilla, the NYPL and the stuffed version of the lovable bear and his pal Christopher Robin, which was inspired by A.A. Milne’s real son, Christopher Robin Milne, and his toy companion.
Queen Camilla Recently Visited the Original Winnie-the-Pooh Display

The British monarch has long professed her love and admiration for the Winnie-the-Pooh story. Instead of having the toy bear come to her, she journeyed across the pond to see the stuffed animal when she visited the New York Public Library in April.
During her trip this spring to the U.S. with King Charles III, she stopped by the library and presented a gift: a Roo doll.
While visiting the library, the queen also read “Winnie-the-Pooh” to a group of children.

“On behalf of the Library and our millions of visitors, we thank Her Majesty Queen Camilla — and we welcome Roo to New York City,” President and CEO of the New York Public Library Anthony W Marx said in a press release at the time. “Roo will help us continue to share the wonder and magic of this timeless story with readers of all ages for generations to come.”

The original baby kangaroo stuffed animal was lost in an apple orchard in the 1930s, the library’s website says. The toy was absent when the rest of the Pooh and friends collection was donated to the library by Dutton Children’s Books in 1987.
Visitors can see the Roo in the Silly Old Bear! Winnie-the-Pooh at 100 display located at the Schwarzman Building until Nov. 30.
A Friend of A.A. Milne’s Son Says Queen Camilla Sent Him to Try to Have Pooh Temporarily Returned to the U.K.
Queen Camilla hasn’t publicly requested Winnie-the-Pooh return to England, but an emissary has done so on her behalf, according to the Washington Post.

Brits have a strong attachment to the teddy bear, which was originally purchased at a Harrods in 1921. The nation has been celebrating the anniversary of his origin story with special editions, commemorative stamps, LEGO sets and a new sequel titled “A Little Boy and His Bear,” according to the Washington Post.

Gyles Brandreth, an author and friend of the late Christopher Robin Milne, told the Washington Post he was sent by Queen Camilla to New York in 2024 as an emissary. Brandreth said the queen wanted him to arrange for Winnie-the-Pooh to temporarily relocate to Buckingham Palace for the 100th anniversary.

Brandreth said the New York Public Library rejected the offer due to the bear’s age and fragility as far as transporting it. Plus, the library stressed how many visitors the Winnie-the-Pooh and Friends collection attracts every year.
“It would be wonderful if it happens, but I can’t see it happening anytime soon,” he said. “The ball is now really in the court of the New York Public Library.”
TODAY.com has reached out to Buckingham Palace and Brandreth respectively for comment but did not immediately hear back.
A spokesperson for The New York Public Library has not confirmed The Washington Post’s report or Queen Camilla’s interest in Winnie-the-Pooh.
Manhattan Boro President Rejects Any Call to Return Pooh and Friends to the U.K.
Manhattan Boro President Brad Hoylman said in an Instagram video that New York City will not be returning the beloved stuffed animals.

“I’m here at the New York Public Library, where apparently an international incident has ensued, because the government of the United Kingdom, through Queen Camilla herself, has requested the return of Winnie-the-Pooh and Friends,” he said while standing by the exhibit at the NYPL.
Camilla has not publicly asked for the bear’s return.
“They are the property of the people of New York,” he said. “They are staying put.”
Text over the video read, “Hands off our Pooh!” The post also included an emoji of a jar of honey, Pooh’s favorite snack.
“The British are coming for Winnie the Pooh,” he wrote in the caption Instagram. “Sorry, Your Majesty. Pooh is a New Yorker.”
He added that the stuffed animals are the third-most popular attraction at the NYPL behind only historic copies of Declaration of Independence and the Bill of Rights.
The NYPL also issued a statement to TODAY.com through director of communications Melissa Grace.

“The New York Public Library has been the proud steward of Winnie-the-Pooh and his friends since 1987, when the dolls were donated to us by Dutton Children’s Books,” Grace said. “On permanent display at our flagship location in Midtown Manhattan, Christopher Robin’s childhood toys are a cornerstone of our renowned children’s literature collection.”
She added, “We’re excited to celebrate the 100th anniversary of Winnie-the-Pooh, and invite everyone to see them up-close in our Treasures exhibition — always for free.”
The British Embassy Denies Report of the U.K. Wanting Pooh to Be Returned
Brandreth’s comments to the Washington Post about being sent by Queen Camilla to broker Pooh’s return to England prompted the British Embassy to issue a denial on Oct. 22.

“Reports of a campaign to return Winnie-the-Pooh to the UK are unfounded,” the embassy said in a statement on X. “It’s great to have Pooh and friends in New York (reunited with Roo at last, thanks to Her Majesty) making new friends and inspiring thousands of children each year.”

The embassy added that “there’s an open invite if Pooh ever wants to make a temporary visit to the UK, but we have no doubt that Pooh and his pals are in excellent hands with the New York Public Library.”
A Dispute Over Pooh Also Happened 28 Years Ago
This is only the latest friendly back-and-forth over where the iconic stuffed animals should be housed.
The White House and British Parliament traded comments back in 1998, leading Rudy Giuliani, the New York City mayor at the time, to say the bear and his friends would be staying put in the Big Apple.
“I think we’re going to keep him here for a while, and keep him safe,” Giuliani said. “We’re getting a little nervous that somebody wants to take him away.”

title: Did Johnny Carson Really Turn Down ‘The Tonight Show’? Watch Him Explain to TODAY in 1983 What Happened
summary: Johnny Carson spoke with TODAY in 1983 about what it’s like hosting “The Tonight Show” and why he initially turned down the chance to host it.
story: Welcome to the “TODAY Archives,” where we revisit memories from our show when celebrities and newsmakers started discourse, made us laugh or shaped our culture. This latest installment features Johnny Carson on Sept. 28, 29, 30 and Oct. 3, 1983, talking all things “The Tonight Show.”

Interviews on TODAY often feature people in the news or those of some cultural import. Imagine, then, just how big you have to be to be interviewed over multiple days spanning two weeks. Such was the case with Johnny Carson, whose chat with Bryant Gumbel aired over a four-episode period on Sept. 28, 29, 30 and Oct. 3, 1983, on the eve of a special 21st anniversary show for “The Tonight Show,” which he had begun hosting in 1962 and would remain until 1992.
It was not necessarily the ideal situation for Carson, who told Gumbel, “I don’t like to be interviewed” because it makes him uncomfortable.
“I guess I’m private, and sometimes I think, well, maybe I’m saying things I shouldn’t,” he added.

Regardless, the man dubbed “The King of Late Night,” who would’ve turned 101 on Oct. 23, sat down with Gumbel for an interview that aired for more than 25 minutes and covered a wide swath of subject matter.
Did Johnny Carson Actually Pass Up Hosting ‘The Tonight Show’ At First?
It seems hard to believe, but Carson did initially reject the offer to host the iconic show.
“I turned it down,” he said, while noting he was hosting an ABC show called “Who Do You Trust” at the time that was “easy” and paying “very good money.”
He eventually relented because of “the challenge” of doing something new.
“If you like television and you’re going to be a performer, then you’ve got to go to the next step,” he said.
That next step ultimately made him a legend. Carson hosted “The Tonight Show” for three decades, a feat he never could have imagined on his first night as host.

“I remember the first night standing backstage, and somebody said, ‘Well, when this is over, it’ll be a week. Then it’ll be a year,’” he said. “Then somebody says, ‘Ten years from now, you won’t even remember this night.’ We all laughed, thinking there’s no way anybody’s going to do this for 10 years.”
What Was His Approach to Hosting ‘The Tonight Show’?
Carson replaced Jack Parr and knew he couldn’t try to do what his predecessor did.
“I realized that there’s no way I could follow Jack Parr by trying to emulate Jack Parr. So you have to really go on and do your own show,” he said.
Carson, who died in 2005 at the age of 79, also said he had to keep things interesting for the audience, even on nights when the magic may not have been there.

“What you try to do is to keep from boring people,” he said. “You don’t come out with any master plan that the show is going to be great because you can’t be good every night. So you have to keep that — I think that little edge. If you don’t, then you start to get ... bored with the show yourself. The audience is going to get bored.”
Who Would Replace Johnny Carson on ‘The Tonight Show’?
Carson was already a legend by the time he sat down with Gumbel, but noted that, “Anybody’s expendable, and I’m not saying that on any false sense of humility.”

“I remember when Parr did the show. Everybody says, ‘Nobody can replace Jack Parr.’ That’s true. Parr was Parr,” Carson said. “Somebody else will come along and do the show. It happened to be me. If I leave the show, they’ll say, ‘All right, nobody’s going to replace Johnny Carson.’ True to that extent, that they will do the show completely different.”
Jay Leno would take over the reins from Carson in 1992 — which is essentially the type of person Carson predicted would replace him.

“I think it takes basically somebody who is a comedian,” he said. “The ones who’ve been successful at it, going back to the days of Jerry Lester, Bernie Kovacs, Parr, Steve Allen, have all been, basically, guys who think funny, I think, can do a certain amount of writing and make observations about things. They have a comedic mind. I think it takes that.”
What Did Johnny Carson Think About Politics and ‘The Tonight Show’?
Today, late-night TV is hyper-focused on politics. And while Carson certainly made jokes about politics in his monologues, he was not interested in booking politicians themselves.

“I think ‘The Tonight Show’ basically is an entertainment show. I’m basically a comedian, a performer. And so politicians, for example, when they come on, I think they find it very difficult,” he said. “They’re there for one reason: either to promote their point of view, or to back or not back the administration and create an image. So it’s very difficult to get underneath and find the person and lighten them up.”
Despite that stance, politics remained a gold mine for his monologues.

“They give you so much material,” he said. “I mean, the government’s a great source of comedy material. What goes on in Washington? You get to pick up the papers every day, and you’ve got something to work from.”

title: ‘The Traitors: New Blood’ Episode 7 Introduces Power to Shake Up the Game
summary: Read a recap of Episode 7 of “The Traitors: New Blood” to find out who went home and what new power was introduced to the game.
story: Warning: Spoilers from Episode 7 of “The Traitors: New Blood” below.
Who knew one apple could lead to three episodes of chaos and confusion?

Two weeks after the first murder in plain sight of “The Traitors: New Blood” was completed, speculation surrounding the Traitors and their connection to the crime will not cease. Although the trio successfully survived banishment last week, the same theory linking Tomica and Joe to Niyyah’s murder resurfaced in Episode 7, which aired on NBC Oct. 22.

At the end of last week’s episode, Victor made it clear that he would continue to voice his suspicions of Tomica to anyone who would listen. But in the new episode, titled “It’s Like Fighting Two Pigs Under A Blanket,” he wasn’t the only Faithful the Traitors had to worry about. As host Alan Cumming revealed in the teaser for this episode, a new power was introduced that could have a major impact on the game.

What is the power and who received it? Read on for a recap of Episode 7 of “The Traitors: New Blood” to find out. Plus, learn if the Traitors decided to murder Victor and if the trio made it through another banishment.
A Murder and Endless Finger-Pointing

The episode began with Katie, Tomica and Joe in the turret contemplating who to murder. Although Tomica pushed for Victor, Katie pointed out that getting rid of him would cause Tomica and Joe to look more suspicious. So, the three decided to include Wyatt, Mark, and Kriste on their shortlist for murder.

The next morning, Victor announced in his confessional that he will not let go of “fruit-gate” and planned to target Tomica. But, he faced an uphill battle as multiple Faithfuls said in their confessionals they didn’t think Victor’s theory was helpful. Plus, Abby L. still didn’t trust Wyatt, and Ben revealed in his confessional that he was wary of Katie.

After all the players arrived at breakfast, it was revealed that Mark was killed. In a flashback to the turret, Joe said Mark needed to be murdered because he was a “full-blown Faithful” and no one suspected him.

When he walked into the confessional and saw a note from the Traitors, Mark said, “Oh my God, I knew this was going to happen. Oh, it’s horrible.” After reading the letter, he added, “Damn, that sucks bro. Killing me was just really not cool but this has been such an unreal experience. I’m so grateful for meeting everyone. And at least I made it way more fun to be here. I would give the Faithful advice but I haven’t been right yet. So, you know, good luck.”

Before the mission, more Faithfuls privately shared their theories, with Kriste worrying about Abby L. repeatedly leading them in the wrong direction and Clyde speculating about Morgan’s unusual behavior.
A Mission and a Mysterious Power
Prior to the mission, Alan warned the players that they would be required to be “outstanding in your field.” He also said the prize pot totaled $97,000.

The players were taken to a large field filled with terrifying scarecrows. There, they had to rip open and sift through the scarecrows’ innards to find unmarked bags of gold. They then had to take the gold and return it to their marked barrows, without knowing the value of each bag.

But Alan had a new twist to share. “In today’s mission, you’re not just playing for gold. You are each playing for a huge new power. This power can turn the entire Round Table on its head,” he revealed. Whoever had the most gold in their barrow at the end of the 15-minute mission would win the power. However, every player wouldn’t make it to the end of the mission as some scarecrows contained black hearts. If a black heart was placed in another player’s barrow, that player would be eliminated.

During the mission, Shane eliminated Victor, Clyde got rid of Morgan, Abby L. put a black heart in Wyatt’s barrow and Ben eliminated Katie. The group added $15,300 to the prize pot, and Alan shared that the power would be revealed later at the Round Table.
A Chaotic Round Table and the Pardon Power
Before the Round Table, Tomica pulled Victor for a private chat to learn why he was fixated on her and his fruit theory. When he asked her to name a person she didn’t trust, Tomica mentioned Katie.

The Round Table started with Kriste calling out Abby L. for consistently being wrong. In response, Abby L. pushed her Wyatt theory, again. Next, Victor spoke up and shifted the conversation to Niyyah’s murder. But, he was shut down after Jay called him a distraction and said he wanted to vote for Victor.
Victor didn’t back down and reiterated his idea that Tomica and Joe are Traitors. To make Tomica look more untrustworthy, he also revealed that she threw Katie under the bus.
In a confessional, Tomica said she mixed up Katie’s name with Kriste’s name by mistake.

During the vote, Katie turned on Tomica and wrote her name, along with Victor and Wyatt. But, it wasn’t enough to send her home. A majority of the players voted to banish Victor. He stood on the Circle of Truth, preparing his exit speech, before Alan interrupted. He said the power he teased earlier is called “The Power of the Pardon” and it could save Victor. The winner of the power can either let the banishment stand or grant Victor mercy.
The episode ended on a cliffhanger before viewers learned who won the power that would decide Victor’s fate.
What Will Happen Next Episode?
In Episode 8, titled “A Bad Apple Spoils the Whole Bunch,” fans will find out if Victor will be saved.
The episode will air Thursday, Oct. 29, on NBC at 8 p.m. ET/ 7 p.m. CT.

title: Miley Cyrus Helps Fan Shave Her Head Before Chemo Treatment: ‘Let’s Go Girl’
summary: Miley Cyrus recently stepped up to help a fan and fellow musician Cash Jacobs during an emotional battle with breast cancer.
story: Miley Cyrus recently stepped up to help a fan during an emotional battle with breast cancer.

The singer met with Cash Jacobs, a fellow musician, after one of her shows at the Hollywood Bowl earlier this month. During their hang, Cyrus helped Jacobs, who has Stage 3 breast cancer, shave her head in preparation for her chemotherapy treatments. The process was captured in a video that was shared on social media Oct. 21. And for Jacobs, the moment was profoundly meaningful.

“thank you @miley. For making me feel safe and comfortable, for giving me your time, and for being exactly who you are,” Jacobs wrote in the post’s caption. “It is a huge gift to continue to watch you grow and you are forever my biggest inspiration. Stay soft and strong 🤍”
In the video, Cyrus gives Jacobs some uplifting advice. The “Flowers” star also says a few words before the makeover.
“Thank you to the universe for bringing us together, and celebrating our connection and what music does for the world — it brings people like you and me together that may never meet,” Cyrus says.
The video then gets into the makeover process.
“Let’s go girl,” Cyrus says, before taking the buzzers to Jacobs’ head.
The pair share some light moments as well, with Cyrus remarking on how great Jacobs looks in the new ‘do.
“You got cute ears, you got a good-shaped head, you got a gorg face,” Cyrus says.

Jacobs initially got connected with Cyrus after she posted a video, sharing her breast cancer journey and calling on the singer to be the one to shave her head. The internet responded by tagging Cyrus and ultimately, the “Malibu” songstress came through.

In her Oct. 21 post, Jacobs explained that Cyrus not only flew her out to Los Angeles and gave her tickets to the show, but also helped her through “one of the scariest and most intimate moments of my life.”
“They say don’t meet your idols. Well I did. And it was everything and more,” Jacobs wrote.
She added that Cyrus’ music has always uplifted her during difficult moments in her life.

“And when they pass, I can listen to her songs and be reminded that I got through it and came out stronger,” Jacobs wrote. “Between major depressive episodes and finding out I have stage 3 breast cancer. I am lucky enough to have reached her and her team and been given this opportunity of a lifetime.”
Jacobs also thanked the internet for making it all happen, before praising Cyrus for her kindness.

“Miley is the softest, coolest, KINDEST, and most genuine human being I’ve ever had the privilege of meeting and spending time with. And not to mention her SHAVING MY F***ING HEAD!!!!! WHAT?!?” Jacobs wrote. “I want to hold on to this moment and to always remember the conversations we had and what they mean for me.”

Cyrus’ two nights at the Hollywood Bowl have been all-around emotional. The singer, whose recent performances marked her first solo shows since 2022, broke down as she paid tribute to her godmother, the late country legend Dolly Parton, on opening night.
“Me and Dolly, we are eternal,” Cyrus said, speaking to the crowd as she sat at the edge of the stage. “Nothing in this life could ever tear us apart.”

title: I’m a Forensic Psychologist Trained to Spot Liars. This Is What I’d Ask Elizabeth Holmes After Watching ‘You Can See Everything’
summary: This is what a forensic psychologist trained to spot liars thinks of Elizabeth Holmes in “You Can See Everything.”
story: “Take it From Me” is a TODAY series where experts use their wisdom to explain trends or make recommendations within their fields. In this edition, a forensic psychologist weighs in on “You Can See Everything.”
Spoilers ahead for “You Can See Everything.”

“You Can See Everything” has audiences twisting to identify truths and lies. Filmmakers Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim moved into Elizabeth Holmes’ house 34 days before she was set to surrender to federal prison for an 11-year sentence related to defrauding investors in relation to her biotech company, Theranos.
John De La Torre, a forensic psychologist who specializes in criminal work, scams and con artists, is uniquely well-suited to weigh in on who was telling the truth among all the players.
But he couldn’t.

“When I left that movie, I left feeling that all I saw was a game,” De La Torre tells TODAY.com. “All I saw was Nathan Fielder’s game to try to show me what he considers to be the truth, but isn’t necessarily the full truth. I see Billy and I see Elizabeth Holmes. I see the games that they play.”
De La Torre is trained to see deception and malingering. But he says this isn’t humans’ strong suit. “We’re not very good at detecting who is lying to us,” he says.
That’s what makes parsing this documentary as an audience member difficult. “Everything that is going on is masked by the color of the possibility that we are being lied to,” he says.
The Questions a Forensic Psychologist Would Have Asked Elizabeth Holmes

If De La Torre were in Fielder’s shoes, he says he would start with talking to Holmes about her defining relationships: “What she understands about them. Are the relationships that she has transactional, and what does that transaction look like for her? How does she know that someone likes her or doesn’t like her?”
While listening, he looks for consistency in people’s stories. “Consistent people tell the truth. Inconsistent people lie,” he says.

He paid attention to Fielder’s lines of questioning. While he’s “pretty good at exploring and following up,” he noticed some of the things he didn’t follow up on, like Holmes’ father’s disclosure of her previous sexual assault.

He also would take an approach similar to his work as a forensic psychologist, De La Torre assesses people accused of a crime using sanity and competency evaluations, to see if there is a mental disorder that a person may have.
Here’s Where He Comes Down on Elizabeth Holmes
After seeing the movie, De La Torre made up his mind about Holmes.
“I think she legitimately thinks she did nothing wrong,” he says. “I’m not even sure she knows.”

“I think she operates under the assumption that she needs to win or that something positive needs to happen. So long as she’s on the positive side, she’s willing to engage in whatever behavior she needs to engage in. That includes potentially making someone else be the bad guy,” she says.
Holmes swears to Fielder that she’s never knowingly told a lie, despite being convicted of fraud in 2022.

For a bit of background, Holmes dropped out of Stanford and became the youngest female billionaire thanks to Theranos, the biotech company she founded, based on a technology that could purportedly run tests on a single drop of blood.

Holmes was convicted on four federal charges of wire fraud for misrepresenting to investors what the Edison blood-testing machine could actually do. In her trial, she denied her product was defective.
Even if she swears she’s not lying, De La Torre considers Holmes a con artist.

“I think she truly believed in the work that she was doing, but therein lies the con because it doesn’t actually do the things that she claimed that it did,” De La Torre says. “She made other people believe that it could already do those things. And it is through that belief, that confidence that she had, that that was the con game that she was playing.”
Ultimately, De La Torre describes Holmes’ con as: “Making someone else believe that they are what she needs in order to be successful.”
What the Shower Scene Says About Billy Evans

Billy Evans, Holmes’ partner with whom she shares two children, has ample screen time in the movie, often intervening and sharing his own opinions. At one point, the camera catches Evans fully nude in the shower. It’s a telling moment, according to De La Torre.
“His willingness to expose himself to another man suggests that what he craves is attention,” he says.
He often gets attention by “saying something outlandish, saying something ridiculous, saying something that clearly demonstrates that he doesn’t care about other people.”
Whereas Holmes often “appears as though she’s executing human programming,” Evans knows how to feel and emote more easily.
The ‘Only Person’ With an Objective View
According to De La Torre, the only person with an objective and unbiased view of the action is Amanda Seyfried.

“It’s important to understand that no one in this film is telling the truth, except for Amanda Seyfried, and the only truth she tells is by calling out all of the other games that are being played whenever anybody is talking,” De La Torre says.

Seyfried played Holmes in the Hulu series “The Dropout,” and reprises the role in the documentary, all while helping Fielder investigate what’s really going on between Holmes and Evans. Her onscreen presence is captivating and animated, acting as a stand-in for the audience.
“I think she’s the one that calls out everything, all of the nonsense whether it’s from Billy or whether it’s from Nathan. I think Amanda Seyfried is the person to really listen to,” he continues.
An Exercise in Confirmation Bias
“You Can See Everything”? More like, “You Can See Some Things, Kind Of.”
De La Torre says that if you walk out of the theater confused, it’s only because you recognize Holmes, Evans and Fielder all had an agenda.
“Every single one of them is playing the game. And leaving confused just tells me that you are now also aware that what you are seeing may not be fully everything, “he says.

title: Daisy Edgar-Jones’ Dad, Who Created ‘Big Brother,’ Gave Her This Talk Before She Got Famous
summary: Daisy Edgar-Jones’ father, a TV executive who co-created Big Brother, gave her this talk before she got famous.
story: British television executive Philip Edgar-Jones witnessed plenty of people rocket to fame while at the helm of the long-running reality show “Big Brother,” so he had some words of wisdom for his daughter when she was on the verge of stardom herself.

Actor Daisy Edgar-Jones, 28, spoke with Jenna Bush Hager on the Oct. 22 episode of her “Open Book with Jenna” podcast about the advice her father gave her before the Emmy-winning series “Normal People” was released in 2020.
She noted how on “Big Brother,” “individuals would come in anonymous and leave very, very famous,” so her father had experience seeing people make that transition during his 10 years with the show.
When “Normal People” was released during the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020, he reached out to her over the phone and on video calls to prepare her for what might lay ahead.

“(He) essentially said, there might be some things that will shift for you, and here’s just some words I’ve learned of wisdom. Which is that you might not change, but the world around you might, and the way people interact with you might, and so remembering that you haven’t changed, that you are who you are and you are the same person that you were pre all of this is really important to keep your feet on the floor.”
“Normal People,” based on a bestselling novel by Sally Rooney, was Edgar-Jones’ breakout role, so the advice was timely.

She said her father advised her to “know that you’re an individual amongst lots of people with all their own stuff going on and inner lives, and it’s really important to remember to keep your feet planted very firmly on the floor.”
The “Sense and Sensibility” star remains “grateful” for those words of wisdom. She also hopes to take a cue from her father in another way.

“Every time I meet anyone who’s worked with my dad, they always say he’s the nicest man in television, which is such a lovely legacy,” she said. “And I’m really proud of him for that. I’m proud of him for so many things, but I suppose if I’ve learned from that, it would be nice if that could be my legacy in some way that when you interact with someone, you leave a nice taste in their mouth or a nice flavor. That would be something I’m very proud of.”

title: ‘Love Is Blind’ Stars Stew and Jax Reveal Where They Stand After Awkward Breakup
summary: “Love Is Blind” Season 11 stars Jax and Stew tell TODAY.com how their relationship has unfolded since the show ended.
story: Warning: Spoilers from “Love Is Blind” Season 11 below…
After her ghosting moment that went viral, Jacqueline “Jax” Guelli decided to reunite with ex-fiancé Scott “Stew” Stewart in the newest episodes of “Love Is Blind” to explain her hasty departure.
So far, the most talked about moment of Season 11 of the Netflix reality dating show has been Jax’s reaction after meeting Stew for the first time.

Following their engagement in the pods, Jax and Stew saw each other face-to-face, and the feelings were no longer mutual. She informed the producers that she wanted to leave the show immediately and return home, without breaking up with Stew in person. Producers told him about her abrupt exit, and shared the news that Jax didn’t want to leave any contact information for Stew.

But in Episode 6, the two had a sit-down in Boston to unpack their broken engagement. Stew asked why Jax didn’t want to have a conversation before leaving. She said she should have spoken to him and he didn’t deserve how she treated him. She also shared that her family and friends encouraged her to chat with him.
Jax then told Stew she expected to be “blown away” by their connection in real life, but she wasn’t.
In response, Stew asked, “Is that our cue to leave?” They had another confusing exit and didn’t appear again in the second batch of episodes.
Stew reveals the status of their relationship in an interview with TODAY.com.

“I think the pods was such an intense experience, and it accelerates relationships so much that I think we both kind of lost our bearing once we got back to the real world,” he says. “I think it just took some time for each of us to resettle, reconnect with our friends and family (and) reconnect with normal life.”
As for where the two currently stand, he says, “Since then we’ve been great friends, and the relationship has continued.”
In a separate interview, Jax clarifies to TODAY.com that it wasn’t the opinions of her friends and family that pushed her to meet Stew on camera.
“We definitely needed to talk. And I was happy and I was excited to see him,” she says.
The two will likely reveal more about how they mended their relationship at the upcoming Season 11 reunion. The date of the reunion has yet to be announced.

title: Craig Melvin Wins His People’s Sexiest Man Alive Poll ... and Gets Crowned on TODAY!
summary: Craig Melvin has won the “hotter than your cup of coffee in the morning” category in the People’s Sexiest Man Alive Readers’ Choice poll.
story: Craig Melvin is hot!
The TODAY co-anchor has won the “hotter than your cup of coffee in the morning” category in the People’s Sexiest Man Alive Readers’ Choice poll.
Craig beat out Michael Strahan, Gio Benitez and Vladimir Duthiers for the title, with readers voting on the question: “Which of these morning hosts is hotter than your first cup of coffee?”

“We we are happy to announce, ladies and gentlemen, that our friend Craig here is officially hotter than a cup of coffee this morning,” Carson Daly announced on the Oct. 22 episode of TODAY. “You have been voted People magazine’s sexiest morning show host.”
Craig was recognized for his feat with a towel with the “sexiest man alive” logo on it, along with a crown and a sash.
“Come on, you’re the king,” Al Roker said.
“Long may you reign,” Savannah Guthrie said.
Carson made a joke that Craig got the towel because the magazine knows he sweats a lot.
“Now we know why he sweats. It’s because he’s so hot,” Savannah said.
Craig, who was playfully egged on to give a speech, took the award in stride.
“Glad it’s over,” he said.
“Thanks to my mom and my wife who voted at least 100, 200 times, for sure,” he added.
His wife, Lindsay Czarniak, was also thrilled with the honor.
“He’s just sexy in everything she does,” she said when she appeared from home on the 3rd hour of TODAY on Oct. 22.
“This doesn’t mean that you have to stop doing things, but it’s sort of like you know everything can get a little sexier, like sexy cooking, right?” she joked.
After some jokes about Craig doing chores around the house while shirtless, Lindsay then turned a little bit more serious.

“One of the things I thought of first was my grandma, she’s going to be so excited because she lives for watching you and this show,” she said. “And I tried to call her this morning because I was like, ‘You’re just not going to believe it.’ And this is really cool.”
She ended with a message for her husband. “I do think you’re sexy, but I am really proud of you because you know you’re sexy at heart, as well,” she said.
Craig was nominated for the honor last month and took it in stride. His co-anchors became some of his biggest cheerleaders, with Savannah Guthrie encouraging viewers to “vote early and often.”
“Am I being punk’d right now?” Craig said on TODAY Sept. 30 of his nomination.
Lindsay also made sure to campaign for him. Craig and Lindsay, who have been married since 2011, share two children, Delano, 12, and Sybil, 9.

“He is an amazing dad, tremendous husband, teammate, partner, always so supportive and encouraging,” she said in an Instagram reel posted Oct. 12. “He makes a mean chili ... he is a pro at candle-making. He is really good at debating. This is true — and I mean in the most positive of ways.
“But beyond that, he is someone who really cares about where he’s from, leaves people feeling really good about themselves in his presence,” she continued.

“And beyond all those things that make him sexy on the outside — like, let’s be honest, the dimple, guys, it’s the dimple — I think it’s his character and his makeup on the inside that make us think that really, you know, he’s the sexiest man alive.”
Craig had previously appeared in People’s Readers’ Choice poll. In 2023, he was nominated for sexiest morning show host, but lost out to Mark Consuelos.

title: How to Read All 18 of Sarah J. Maas’ Books In Order
summary: So you’re considering jumping down the rabbit hole that is author Sarah J. Maas’ sprawling catalog of romantasy books.
story: So you’re considering jumping down the rabbit hole that is author Sarah J. Maas’ sprawling catalog of romantasy books. You’ve heard about her, perhaps through BookTok or your reading buddies or her legions of fans who can’t get enough. You know about her three series — “Throne of Glass,” “A Court of Thorns and Roses” and “Crescent City”— and her forthcoming books, “A Court of Splintered Harmony” and “A Court of Forgotten Melody,” have only heightened your interest.
So you want to join in on the fun. But where do you begin? And what order should you be reading?
If you’re overwhelmed — 18 books might do that — fret not. We’ll help you get started.
More on Sarah J. Maas and ‘ACOTAR’
Sarah J. Maas Is BookTok’s Reigning Romantasy Queen. All Rise‘A Court of Thorns and Roses’ Books 6 and 7 Titles and Covers Revealed by Sarah J. Maas
Sarah J. Maas Is BookTok’s Reigning Romantasy Queen. All Rise
‘A Court of Thorns and Roses’ Books 6 and 7 Titles and Covers Revealed by Sarah J. Maas
Sarah J. Maas Books to Read First
There are two key things to note when getting started:
It doesn’t matter if you read the “Throne of Glass” books or the “ACOTAR” books first.
Read the “ACOTAR” books before you pick up the “Crescent City” books.

If you’re debating whether to start with “Throne of Glass” or “ACOTAR,” it depends on your preference: “ACOTAR” is romance forward — if you lean toward that genre, start there. “Throne of Glass” is big on the epic fantasy elements — you lean toward that, start there.
‘Throne of Glass’ Series Reading Order
